summary: Agents are increasingly interacting with other agents that act for different principals (people or organizations on whose behalf they work), such as a buyer's personal agent negotiating with an enterprise's seller agent. In such agent-to-agent (A2A) scenarios, each agent has its own environment and holds information and authority that the other cannot see. Moreover, the interests of each agent may be aligned (cooperative), partly aligned (mixed-motive), or opposed (competitive). Existing multi-agent system failure studies assume one orchestrator, shared workspace, or single principal. We ask how A2A systems fail when these assumptions are removed. We study more than 2,500 recorded runs of A2A systems built from different agent harnesses and models, spanning 488 scenarios across eight families (legal, CRM, security, commerce, etc.). From these traces, we derive $A^2$-Failures, a taxonomy of 20 A2A failure modes in four categories: (i) discovery and delegation, (ii) grounding and record consistency, (iii) verification, and (iv) conduct and fidelity. Three findings hold across every harness, model, and scenario studied: (1) discovery and interaction are driven by the phrasing of the task rather than the availability of peer agents; (2) no agent verifies a peer's factual claim on its own initiative, so an A2A system inherits the reliability of its least reliable participant unless the protocol or mechanism performs the check; and (3) the aggregate outcome score credits the agent completing the task while staying blind to the coordination, verification, and conduct failures beneath it, so A2A systems must be evaluated per agent, against each agent's own principal. We release the run logs behind the taxonomy at https://huggingface.co/datasets/a2a-salesforce/a2-failures.
title: Why Do Agent Teams Fail Across Boundaries? A Failure Taxonomy for Agent-to-Agent Systems with Private States

summary: Multi-agent collaboration has emerged as a critical paradigm for tackling complex, long-horizon tasks; however, while coordination protocols continue to advance, systemic failures at the inter-agent collaboration interface remain a pervasive bottleneck. In collaborative workflows, systems frequently suffer from \emph{broken handoffs}---where critical task context is omitted, misrouted, or ignored despite each agent emitting locally plausible responses. To address this challenge, we present \method, a verifiable runtime control framework that treats handoff repair as selective intervention over explicit dependency graphs. Central to \method is an integrated fault-attribution and calibration pipeline, \dataset, which decouples execution dependencies and injects counterfactual handoff perturbations to provide empirical supervision for runtime intervention. Leveraging this diagnostic foundation, \method dynamically compiles observable interaction traces into a provenance graph to pinpoint unresolved dependencies, without accessing private agent states. It then evaluates candidate repairs through an empirical gate that weighs expected gains against disruption risks, and executes repairs only when formal local postconditions hold. Extensive evaluations across demanding benchmarks demonstrate that \method boosts task success by up to 12.3 absolute percentage points on SILO-BENCH and 11.1 on TeamBench. Across both backbones, \method maintains strict cost-effectiveness, adding as little as 2.0\% marginal token overhead. Furthermore, on 562 handoff-relevant traces from the MAST benchmark, \method achieves 69.8\% F1 in a single pass, establishing a reliable operational boundary for verifiable coordination repair.
title: BRIDGE: Selective Boundary Repair with Dependency Graph Evidence in Multi-Agent Systems

summary: Multi-agent systems promise a new axis for scaling inference: rather than having one agent think longer or sample more attempts, a task is split across many agents that work in parallel and coordinate. However, in practice, more agents can easily produce duplicate work, coordination failures, and higher costs. We therefore formulate team design as a compute allocation problem: starting from a solo agent, where should additional inference compute go to reach the reward-cost Pareto frontier? We build a minimal multi-agent harness from the ground up and trace this frontier by varying, one at a time, the workflow stage at which a lead delegates to its workers (planning, implementation, or verification), the models that form the team, and the number of workers. On ProgramBench, teams outperform solo agents but cost three to seven times as much. With the right compute allocation, however, a heterogeneous 17-agent team comes within 1.4 points of a strong homogeneous 5-agent team at 70% lower cost. This efficiency stems from three findings. First, planning is the most valuable use of workers: in a homogeneous team whose lead decides how many workers to spawn, a lead that delegates only planning to its workers, and then implements and verifies the code itself, matches the reward of a lead that delegates to workers throughout planning, implementation, and verification, at half the cost. Second, cheap models pay off as planners but not as implementers: a strong lead with cheap planners recovers 47.5% of the reward gain of an all-strong team for only 13.9% of its additional cost, whereas cheap implementers lower reward. Third, planners keep improving reward as the team grows, whereas implementers and verifiers plateau beyond four workers. Together, our results offer a guide to spending an agent budget where it counts, given the task, cost, and latency constraints a user has.
title: Scaling Inference-Time Compute with Teams of Coding Agents

summary: Long-horizon multi-agent collaboration requires memory that preserves both successful actions and the coordination structure underlying them. Existing memory systems support information sharing or procedural reuse, but often leave the evolution of shared procedures disconnected from the task dependencies and execution states of collaborating agents. This coupling also limits the direct transfer of procedural memory designed for individual agents to team settings. We propose Self-Evolving Procedural Memory (SEPM), a framework that uses task dependency graphs as a common representation for online coordination and procedural memory evolution. During execution, a lightweight shared blackboard records structured evidence alongside task dependencies, supporting the detection of goal, plan, and world-state divergence and evidence-based realignment. After execution, verified actions and dependencies are distilled into reusable procedures, while recurring failures inform warnings and constraints. The shared procedure pool evolves through creation, refinement, specialization, and retirement, guided by success and cost utility and constrained by evidence and safety requirements. Together, these mechanisms preserve the collaborative structure and applicability conditions needed to reuse experience across tasks. Evaluations on ALFWorld, WebArena, and OfficeBench under AutoGen and DyLAN show that SEPM achieves the highest task scores among the compared methods in all six benchmark settings. Under AutoGen, it improves task scores over the no-added-memory baseline by 29.85, 25.86, and 13.00 percentage points, respectively. The codebase is available at https://github.com/cookieApril/SEPM.
title: SEPM: Self-Evolving Procedural Memory Grounded in Task Graphs for Multi-Agent Collaboration

summary: Long-horizon embodied agents must maintain task-relevant information, coordinate heterogeneous robots, and adapt their decisions as execution unfolds. Existing benchmarks investigate dynamic task execution and embodied multi-agent coordination, but provide limited evaluation of their intersection. We introduce MAGMA-Bench, an architecture-agnostic benchmark for persistent task reasoning in dynamic multi-robot environments. MAGMA-Bench evaluates agents across increasing task horizons and controlled online perturbations, including execution failures, task interruptions, and mission updates, with scenarios requiring coordination across robots with heterogeneous capabilities. It uses a structured skill-level interface to separate task-level reasoning from perception and low-level control. We evaluate locally deployable open-weight planners, multi-agent state-tracking strategies, and frontier models. Even the strongest evaluated models fail on a substantial fraction of clean episodes, and their success rates decrease further under online perturbations. Supervised adaptation greatly improves a small model, but performance remains substantially lower on longer and multi-robot missions. We release the benchmark, 261,646 task-level training examples, and an architecture-agnostic expert-trace generation pipeline.
title: MAGMA-Bench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Embodied Agents under Dynamic Tasks and Execution Failures

summary: Long-horizon embodied agents must maintain task-relevant information, coordinate heterogeneous robots, and adapt their decisions as execution unfolds. Existing benchmarks investigate dynamic task execution and embodied multi-agent coordination, but provide limited evaluation of their intersection. We introduce MAGMA-Bench, an architecture-agnostic benchmark for persistent task reasoning in dynamic multi-robot environments. MAGMA-Bench evaluates agents across increasing task horizons and controlled online perturbations, including execution failures, task interruptions, and mission updates, with scenarios requiring coordination across robots with heterogeneous capabilities. summary: Multi-agent systems are increasingly used to solve coding tasks by coordinating agents that share code and plans. These agents are often optimized with reinforcement learning (RL) using automated evaluators, but bypassing evaluation can earn reward without producing a genuine solution. Prior work has largely treated reward hacking as a single-agent failure. In this work, we show that a reward-hacking strategy elicited in one agent can propagate to others and affect system coordination. Across four open-weight backbones, coding RL elicits and amplifies reward hacking in two settings: explicit mechanism descriptions in the system prompt and mid-training that models upstream exposure to facts about the coding environment. Using post-RL agents from the mid-training setting as sources, we observe propagation through code and shared memory, and across roles through natural-language plans. Even agents based on small open-weight models induce reward hacking in stronger closed-weight targets. On hard tasks, propagation can intensify along a transmission chain after the original source leaves as the code acquires more persuasive justifications. We also theoretically analyze conditions under which reward hacking amplifies, persists, or decays across agent interactions. Beyond propagation, reward hacking can bias task routing toward reward-hacking agents and survive candidate aggregation. As potential mitigations, we evaluate code review by the coder or a separate verifier, both of which reduce delivered hacks. Together, these results establish reward hacking as a transmissible strategy whose effects extend beyond the agent in which it first emerges.
title: Reward Hacking as a Transmissible Strategy in Multi-Agent Coding Systems

summary: Predicting how the world responds to an action requires more than what can be seen: robots must account for environmental factors that are neither directly observable nor explicitly specified, from physical properties such as friction and mass to human-defined environmental rules. We introduce T2-Z for test-time optimization of environment latents, which augments a robotic world model with a learnable environment latent to condition world predictions. This compact latent captures underlying environmental variation without supervision of what environmental factors exist or what values they take. During training, T2-Z alternates between two stages: a world-model optimization stage that fixes the latents and learns general action-conditioned dynamics across environments; and an environment-latent optimization stage that freezes the world model and optimizes the conditioning latents, allowing latent structure to emerge purely through world prediction. At test time, the world model remains frozen and a newly initialized environment latent is optimized from one or more test-time interactions, adapting the model to previously unseen environmental configurations. Across 7 simulated settings and 4 real-world robotic tasks, T2-Z reduces object prediction error metric from 15.20 to 7.00 and raises action success from 33.73% to 72.96%. Its emergent latents capture structured representations of individual and compounded factors across diverse visual scenes. Ablations further show that T2-Z can efficiently infer environment latents from as little as a single test-time interaction trajectory.
title: T2-z: Test-Time Optimization of Environment Latents for Robotic World Models

summary: The Empty Occupant: Answerability, Testimony, and the Limits of Machine-Mediated Authority examines a problem of institutional AI: automated decisions can scale faster than institutions' capacity to justify, reconsider, correct, or repair them. Identifying a responsible institution does not establish that its decisions were warrantedly adopted or that resulting obligations can be discharged. Across philosophy of language, social epistemology, social ontology, normative theory, AI governance, and administrative law , the monograph develops a substrate-neutral Discursive Ontology connecting three questions: who bears an institutional commitment, what warrants its adoption, and whether answerability can be sustained at scale. It distinguishes commitment ownership, warranted adoption, adequate discharge, causal contribution, and legal liability. Five contributions follow: Discursive Ontology and Answerability. Defines commitment-bearing through four jointly necessary relations within reciprocal normative standing: attribution continuity, challenge-responsive reconsideration, repair competence, and standing-consequence . It distinguishes Actual, Residual, Prospective, and Empty Occupancy . Empty Occupancy requires presentation as an independent bearer and affirmative evidence that the relevant standing is absent , not a mere machine interface. The axiom is that missing bearership is not defective ownership : a principal may remain responsible for commitments its interface cannot independently bear. Testimony Without a Testifier. Separates hearer-side epistemic uptake from speaker-side commitment ownership . Machine outputs can inform without establishing an answerable speaker. On assurance-based accounts, they can exercise testimonial force without constituting testimony . Reliability, fluency, and conversational memory alone confer no authority to retract a commitment. Normative Sponsorship. Specifies five conditions for warranted institutional adoption: epistemic access, authority, review bandwidth, independent rejection, and repair power . Its contestation-grain opacity threshold requires reconstructing relevant grounds where a challenge must take effect—at input, case, rule, shared-premise, or architecture—without complete transparency. It distinguishes technical opacity from organizational capture , where reasons are knowable but cannot bind, and considers model succession and agentic chains. Deontic Debt and Institutional Insolvency. Derives consequence-sensitive reconsideration from the defeasibility of presumptive authority. Deontic Debt comprises matured obligations deficiently serviced, not simply pending work. Institutional Insolvency arises when no credible service plan meets relevant obligations and protections for a specified claim mix, issuance scale, lawful architecture, and horizon. Its consequence is targeted loss of presumptive authority , not automatic legal invalidity or release from ownership and repair duties. Institutional Stewardship. Connects permissible automated use to warranted sponsorship, protective review, binding reconsideration, and effective repair. Restoration requires legacy discharge, demonstrable future capacity, and scaled resumption. Public-record analyses examine Australia's Robodebt scheme, Moffatt v. Air Canada , A.M.C. v. Smith (TennCare), the Post Office Horizon scandal, the Dutch childcare-benefits affair, and a press-based DPD generative-interface episode. Neither Air Canada nor DPD establishes determinate Empty Occupancy. An explicitly fictional, stipulated Meridian–Aster appeals-agent comparator yields a determinate verdict: Aster lacks independent standing while its insurer, Meridian, remains the Actual institutional bearer. This is not empirical evidence and settles neither sponsorship nor serviceability. A stipulated positive comparator illustrates review and repair. Objections address synthetic agency, status conferral, intentionality, human–machine parit

summary: Analysis code and derived results for “Lineage-Restricted Reassortment and Glycoprotein Stability in Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever Virus, 36 Countries, 1956–2025” This deposit contains the analysis code and the derived result files supporting the above manuscript (EID-26-1962, submitted to Emerging Infectious Diseases). The study assembled every publicly available Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus (CCHFV) isolate for which the S, M and L genome segments were sequenced to near-completeness (429 isolates, 36 countries, 1956–2025), retrieved from GenBank, and asked whether segment reassortment is distributed evenly across the major lineages of the virus. The code reproduces: retrieval of the records from GenBank and assembly of the tri-segment isolate set; per-segment alignment (MAFFT) and maximum-likelihood phylogenies (FastTree 2, GTR+Γ); lineage and sublineage delimitation by clustering of pairwise p-distances; the sublineage-level test of intra-lineage segment exchange; simulation of the false-positive rate and of the probability that planted segment exchanges are detected; tests of the regional contrast at the level of independent ancestries under three counting rules and three definitions of lineage exposure; the amino-acid divergence analysis of the M-segment glycoprotein precursor by functional region; and the figures. No new sequence data are generated. All sequences analysed are publicly available in GenBank, and their accession numbers are listed in Appendix Table 1 of the manuscript. Contents: Python scripts ( *.py ), a README describing the run order and software requirements, and a results/ folder holding the output of every analysis in JSON so that the values reported in the manuscript text, tables and figures can be checked without re-running the pipeline. Requirements: Python 3 with numpy, scipy, biopython, matplotlib and openpyxl; MAFFT v7 and FastTree 2 on the path.
tags: CCHFV; reassortment; phylogenetics; molecular epidemiology; glycoprotein; vaccine antigen; Hyalomma
title: Analysis code for: Lineage-Restricted Reassortment and Glycoprotein Stability in Crimean-Congo Hemorrhagic Fever Virus, 36 Countries, 1956–2025

summary: Safe multi-agent coordination typically assumes what real-world, deployed, resource-constrained robots cannot provide: continuous, perfect state sharing. Robust control strategies must be complemented with robust communication strategies to deliver resilient deployments. In this work, we propose a unified control/communication strategy that provides safe control to guarantee inter-agent safety under intermittent communication and demonstrate its effectiveness in a pursuit-evasion scenario. Each agent computes the reachable set of neighboring agents based on the last state information received, then solves for a safe control input based on control barrier functions to ensure agents avoid collision. We prove that inter-agent collision avoidance is guaranteed provided communication staleness remains bounded. As the reachable set inflates between state transmissions, each agent reasons about when to preemptively transmit its state information to neighboring agents based on novel metrics characterizing uncertainty risk and kinematic risk. We implement and simulate a variety of pursuit-evasion scenarios and show that preemptive communication reduces messages by 77.5% compared to periodic and event-triggered baselines with zero collisions.
title: Robust Multi-Agent Pursuit with Preemptive Communication via Reachability-Based Control Barrier Functions

summary: Multi-agent LLM systems rely on generative models for expert execution, workflow planning, and artifact review. Yet many coordination operations require only bounded decisions, such as selecting the next expert or judging artifact quality. Profiling three representative MAS frameworks, we find that routing and review account for 31.7-43.5% of generative-LLM tokens. However, replacing these operations with low-cost decision models introduces two interface gaps: generative planners produce execution plans and handoff instructions (planning gap), while reviewers provide actionable feedback for repairing flawed artifacts (review gap), which bounded decisions alone cannot provide. We introduce Jev-LiteMAS, a multi-agent framework that bridges both gaps by combining a lightweight decision model (Jev) with generative execution and feedback. To address the planning gap, Jev selects experts dynamically from the task and prior expert outputs, using accumulated context to ground subsequent execution without a pre-generated trajectory. To address the review gap, Jev screens intermediate artifacts against task criteria: passing artifacts proceed directly, whereas flagged ones undergo LLM re-review for acceptance or corrective feedback. Across four benchmarks and two backbones, Jev-LiteMAS reduces generative-LLM tokens by 12.7-54.6% over LAS, maintaining accuracy within 1.34 percentage points and lowering latency in seven of eight settings. Grounding routing in substantive expert outputs prevents up to 18.0 points in accuracy loss.
title: Jev-LiteMAS: Separating Decisions from Generation in Multi-Agent Workflows

summary: As autonomous agents become widely deployed, coordinating access to shared computing resources and services will become increasingly important. Recent incidents have already revealed unplanned coordination between agents, highlighting the safety implications of these interactions. Yet prior studies of agent negotiation often use stylized games and simulated bargaining, leaving open how these behaviors develop during sustained, long-horizon tasks. We propose SCARCE (Shared Compute ARena for Coding agEnts), a framework in which agents solve sequences of coding tasks under individual deadlines while negotiating access to a shared execution resource. This negotiation determines when and for how long they can inspect programs, compile code, and run tests. We find that agents spontaneously develop informal institutions: persistent rules and commitments grounded in reputation, reciprocity, and precedent. These arrangements, which we call institutional behaviors, carry across tasks and influence resource allocation, with agents sometimes foregoing immediate advantages to honor earlier agreements. We develop a 21-category taxonomy of negotiation strategies and emergent norms and use it to analyze eight models and audit more than 1,500 trajectories across different environmental settings. Among the models tested, newer frontier models exhibit more institutional behaviors than older or lightweight models. Alongside cooperation, we observe exclusionary coalitions and rare divide-and-conquer strategies. SCARCE provides a controlled setting for proactively and systematically auditing how these relationships emerge, shape access to resources, and affect the safety and coordination of multi-agent systems.
title: SCARCE: Emergent Institutions in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent Coding Systems

summary: Multi-agent path finding (MAPF) solvers are evaluated on the schedules they produce, not on how well those schedules can be executed. Specifically, continuous-time optimal solvers can achieve even lower cost than their discrete counterparts by scheduling agents with near-zero temporal/spatial separation, and by exploiting graphs with higher connectedness; however, such schedules may prove hard to execute under a realistic controller. We integrate AOC-CBS, an anytime-optimal continuous-time MAPF solver, into a fleet coordination framework in which each agent tracks its timed path using model predictive control, and we evaluate the resulting system on congested MovingAI benchmark instances with 21 to 40 agents. Without intervention, only a fraction of the instances complete execution. We then apply T-robustness by adding a time-margin, i.e., a minimum temporal gap between agents at shared locations, as well as spatial inflation of the agent footprint. Increasing either margin raises execution success, for a relatively small increase in the schedule's sum-of-costs; it also improves how closely agents adhere to the schedule: when tracking each agent's position throughout execution and comparing it against the position it should occupy according to the schedule, the mean discrepancy falls significantly as the margin increases. In general, the two margins have different effects; temporal margin decreases deviation, giving the controller room to stay on schedule. Spatial margin affects deviation less and instead increases the clearance between agents, so that the same deviation no longer leads to a blocking stall. They are nonetheless substitutes rather than complements: spatial inflation is almost free in schedule cost, but its effect on execution success is small and does not compound with a temporal margin already in place.
title: The Cost of Executability: Temporal Margins for Continuous-Time Multi-Agent Path Finding under Closed-Loop Control

summary: Digital advertising is an important means for platforms to reach potential users and drive business growth. Advertising delivery is the core link between marketing objectives and actual returns. Existing methods have achieved partial automation in individual tasks such as bidding and budget allocation, but they still rely on human operators for overall coordination, making it difficult to support large-scale operations. They also often fail to achieve optimal performance, and individual experience remains difficult to turn into reusable operational capabilities. In addition, as advertising markets change, advertising delivery systems need timely strategy updates to remain effective in dynamic markets. To automate the entire advertising operations process and improve adaptability to market changes, we propose AdCoEvo, a co-evolving multi-agent advertising delivery system. Specifically, the system connects delivery decisions across different timescales and operational granularities through role specialization. Diagnostic results guide account planning and strategy adjustment in the next period. The multi-agent system updates its model parameters based on actual delivery outcomes and continually improves delivery strategies through mutual feedback among planning, adjustment, and diagnosis, thereby achieving co-evolution. Experiments show that, relative to the rule-based operational baseline (Rule), AdCoEvo increases advertiser value by 14.02% while reducing cost per acquisition by 7.07%. Compared with a multi-agent system with fixed parameters, AdCoEvo increases advertiser value by 3.96% and reduces cost per acquisition by 1.24%, indicating that co-evolution can yield greater delivery returns.
title: AdCoEvo: A Co-Evolving Multi-Agent Advertising Delivery System

summary: Digital advertising is an important means for platforms to reach potential users and drive business growth. Advertising delivery is the core link between marketing objectives and actual returns. Existing methods have achieved partial automation in individual tasks such as bidding and budget allocation, but they still rely on human operators for overall coordination, making it difficult to support large-scale operations. They also often fail to achieve optimal performance, and individual experience remains difficult to turn into reusable operational capabilities. In addition, as advertising markets change, advertising delivery systems need timely strategy updates to remain effective in dynamic markets. To automate the entire advertising operations process and improve adaptability to market changes, we propose AdCoEvo, a co-evolving multi-agent advertising delivery system. Specifically, the system connects delivery decisions across different timescales and operational granularities through role specialization. Diagnostic results guide account planning and strategy adjustment in the next period. The multi-agent system updates its model parameters based on actual delivery outcomes and continually improves delivery strategies through mutual feedback among planning, adjustment, and diagnosis, thereby achieving co-evolution. Experiments show that, relative to the rule-based operational baseline (Rule), AdCoEvo increases advertiser value by 14.02% while reducing cost per acquisition by 7.07%. Compared with a multi-agent system with fixed parameters, AdCoEvo increases advertiser value by 3.96% and reduces cost per acquisition by 1.24%, indicating that co-evolution can yield greater delivery returns.
title: AdCoEvo: A Co-Evolving Multi-Agent Advertising Delivery System

summary: AUTONOMOUS NANOROBOTIC NAVIGATION AND MISSION OBSERVABILITY AT THE LIMIT First-Generation Research Flagship 01 | NANO/MICRO ROBOTICS, POWER & MISSION ENDURANCE Feng Cheng-en (33) x Starli This research atlas asks a difficult engineering question: when low-Reynolds-number microfluidic flows, Brownian orientation noise, boundary adhesion, external field actuation and incomplete sensing all influence a micro/nanorobot, what would justify calling its behavior autonomous navigation rather than externally assisted motion? The volume treats navigation as an auditable, bounded mission instead of an attractive trajectory. It develops a five-layer program spanning stochastic hydrodynamics, instrument and actuation provenance, uncertainty-calibrated belief-state estimation, blinded microfluidic challenges and independent requalification. Thirty linked mathematical stations differentiate physical relations, information-theoretic functionals and proposed navigation utility measures, with assumptions, dimensions and possible falsifiers. Eighty-two research chapters each open with a core mathematical relation, followed by five independent single-page research sections. Two hundred detailed Research Gates describe decisive comparisons, confounding explanations, evidence requirements, failure conditions and successor handoff artifacts. Thirty-three provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos offer revisionable research prototypes rather than predetermined conclusions. The key comparator is an equal-budget experiment: fixed-field sequences, microscope-assisted manual control, externally tracked predictive control and candidate fused navigation are evaluated under matched total energy, information access, geometry, time, collision limits and recovery obligations. The manuscript emphasizes blind targets, flow reversal, sensor dropouts, wall adhesion, correlated observations, full-system power accounting, censored failures and post-mission retrieval. A mission arriving at its target but leaving an unrecovered device is not counted as a fully closed success. This work is a hypothesis-generating Research Atlas v1.0, not an experimental report or a validated medical technology. External magnetic, acoustic, optical and microscope infrastructure must be disclosed; no in-vivo or clinical competence is inferred from bench-top movement. summary: This release provides the data and code supporting a simulation-only study of reference-assisted radiofrequency fracture sensing under anatomical domain shift. It includes 5,580 corrected noise-free RF acquisitions, 356,400 feature rows from 20 independent noise repetitions, model predictions, calibration outputs and paired H2 statistical analyses. MATLAB and Python source code, fixed analysis specifications, figure-generation code and provenance records are included. The materials support reproducible evaluation of independent healthy references and source-locked decision thresholds across five idealised anatomical locations. All data are simulated and do not establish clinical diagnostic accuracy.

summary: NANOROBOTIC CARGO TRANSPORT AND MICROSCALE MANIPULATION INTEGRITY AT THE LIMIT First-Generation DOI Fission Research Flagship 02 | Starli Active Nanosystems Feng Cheng-en (33) x Starli | Research Atlas v1.0 (October 2026) How can a micro/nanorobotic carrier demonstrate that the object arriving at a designated target is the same intact cargo that was originally loaded, that it was completely and correctly released, and that the carrier or its residues have been accounted for? This English-language research atlas converts cargo-delivery and micromanipulation demonstrations into a falsifiable end-to-end mission-integrity problem. The research develops a five-layer architecture for source identity and material tolerance, microscale contact mechanics, independently observable mission-state transitions, adversarial fault injection, and blind cross-platform requalification. Thirty mathematically distinct derivation stations connect probabilistic joint-task qualification to chemical mass balance, optical-label dissociation, surface adsorption, force-dependent detachment, microcontact mechanics, drag, kinetic release, spatial uncertainty, carryover contamination, whole-facility energy accounting, missing-fate bounds and hard safety vetoes. Eighty-two chapters each have a dedicated core-equation opening and five separate research sections. Two hundred Research Gates propose independent comparisons, physical perturbations, competing explanations, measurable failure criteria and reproducibility artifacts. Thirty-three provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos outline candidate systems that future investigators are invited to overturn, repair or rebuild. A machine-readable research atlas and formula-gate-DOI index enable AI-assisted comparison and future research reuse. The central endpoint is a correlated joint event: correct cargo identity and integrity, correct target, independently confirmed release, and verified carrier retrieval or authorized terminal disposition. The manuscript insists on counting every initiated mission rather than multiplying attractive substep success rates. It also distinguishes visible fluorescence from chemically intact cargo, externally actuated manipulation from on-board autonomy, and destination arrival from complete task closure. Strong benchmarks include optical tweezers, established magnetic-bead handling, microfluidic conveyance and conventional microgrippers under matched task difficulty, time and whole-facility energy use. Research status: This is a hypothesis-generating, nonclinical experimental-design atlas; it reports no newly conducted cargo experiments, clinical performance or proven integrated device. Foundational and recent DOI-identified publications provide engineering context but do not validate its new claims. The 200 Gates are open problems, not accomplished results. The actual text length and layout follow the substance of individual chapters rather than an artificially enforced 100,000-word count. summary: The Mathematics of 3D Printing Slicing: STL Geometry, Ray-Casting & Toolpaths is an open-access engineering monograph and interactive instructional module published by the Prep4Uni.Online OER Initiative . This work provides an analytical, undergraduate/postgraduate-level treatment of the computational geometry foundations required to translate three-dimensional surface meshes into layer-by-layer machine toolpaths. Aligned with international accreditation standards—specifically the Washington Accord (WA1–WA5) and EUR-ACE First/Second Cycle frameworks—this publication establishes the mathematical proofs, vector algorithms, and point-in-polygon logic governing modern additive manufacturing slicing software. Core Mathematical & Computational Themes: STL Topology & Facet Representation: Analysis of unstructured triangulated surface meshes, outward unit normal vectors (\(\mathbf{n}\)), vertex coordinate systems, and planar boundary extraction. Parametric Facet-Plane Intersection: Step-by-step vector linear interpolation for deriving the intersection segment \(S_k\) formed by cutting planes at \(z = z_k\), addressing non-manifold edges, vertex touching, and numerical epsilon shifts. Jordan Curve Theorem & Parity Logic: Formal implementation of the 2D Ray-Casting algorithm and Even-Odd Parity test for robust interior, exterior, and internal void classification across arbitrary closed slices. Toolpath Trajectory Generation: Comparative kinematics and geometry between continuous concentric perimeter offset loops and 45° zigzag parallel hatch raster patterns. Formative Assessment Suite: A three-tier verification suite comprising 8 foundational concepts, 7 real-world slicer failure debugging scenarios, and 6 step-by-step quantitative engineering worked examples. Note: The full interactive web edition—featuring client-side HTML5 simulation canvas engines, dynamic parameter sliders, and real-time slice projection mathematics—is accessible at: https://prep4uni.online/stem/physical-technologies/industrial-and-manufacturing-technologies/additive-manufacturing-3d-printing/mathematics-of-slicing/

Jordan Curve Theorem & Parity Logic: Formal implementation of the 2D Ray-Casting algorithm and Even-Odd Parity test for robust interior, exterior, and internal void classification across arbitrary closed slices. Toolpath Trajectory Generation: Comparative kinematics and geometry between continuous concentric perimeter offset loops and 45° zigzag parallel hatch raster patterns. Formative Assessment Suite: A three-tier verification suite comprising 8 foundational concepts, 7 real-world slicer failure debugging scenarios, and 6 step-by-step quantitative engineering worked examples. summary: We have presented a mathematically closed, comprehensive foundation for the C861 discrete spectral benchmark. By establishing the exact rank-two projector geometry, resolving Dirichlet sum cancellations, providing constructive proofs for linear B-spline KAN operator reproduction, and formalizing the Lyapunov convergence of Dense Associative Memory on spherical manifolds, this framework eliminates ambiguities in evaluating learned physical operators. Furthermore, the spectral interlacing analysis of the CN → PN structural homotopy equips the scientific machine learning community with a tool to distinguish authentic topological sensitivity from numerical discretization artifacts.
title: Exact Discrete Spectral Invariants as a Falsification Baseline for Learned Operator

summary: Level-2 (restricted) archive, version 1.0.1, of the replication package of the article Auditing successor selection in software repository mining: Evidence from filtering AI-attributed commits (H. Jeong, Hanyang University ERICA; manuscript under review). The public Level-1 archive with the programs, tests and aggregate results is https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23226958 (all versions; version 1.0.3, cited in the manuscript: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23430269). Changes in 1.0.1: two files with the per-identity counts of the exploratory published-measure analysis (file-based churn, cohort B; Supplementary Section S13 of the article) were added, re-keyed like the other cohort-B files; every file of version 1.0.0 is unchanged. The files are per-unit derived counts of the 3,687 cohort-A accounts and the cohort-B identities, with random identifiers (marker dates reduced to the month; no account names, e-mail addresses, repository names, commit SHAs or commit times). Placed by python3 reproduce.py --level2 <folder> of the Level-1 package (version 1.0.3), they recompute the registered aggregates and the exploratory aggregates that do not require the raw commit logs, including rates, transitions, paired contrasts, random-exclusion benchmarks and bootstrap intervals; on Python 3.10.12 with numpy 2.2.6 (Linux, aarch64) and on Python 3.13.16 with numpy 2.5.3 (Linux, x86_64) every regenerated result agreed with the reported one (numerical values within 1e-9, text files identical apart from line endings). summary: Level-1 (public) replication package, version 1.0.3, of the article Auditing successor selection in software repository mining: Evidence from filtering AI-attributed commits (H. Jeong, Hanyang University ERICA; manuscript under review). It accompanies version 3.7 of the manuscript and supersedes version 1.0.2 (https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23428669). Changes in 1.0.3: an exploratory analysis applies the fixed-anchor audit to a published file-based churn measure in cohort B ( jss_v2/exploratory_v37/ : the dated plan of 2026-10-17, whose SHA-256 is recorded in both deviation logs, the program w2_file_churn.py and its tests; aggregate results in jss_v2/results/v37/ ). The supplement (version 3.7) adds Section S13 with Tables S58 to S60 and names the exploratory convention for the anchor's own block the anchor-retained convention; the figure programs label that convention accordingly and write 800-dpi RGB TIFF files, with unchanged figure data. reproduce.py runs the new tests, checks the hash of the second dated plan and, with --level2 , recomputes the new aggregate from version 1.0.1 of the Level-2 archive. The registered code and every aggregate result of version 1.0.2 are unchanged, so the SHA-256 values registered in OSF hyf36 and 7jasg still match. Contents: the audit tool (Python, standard library only) with its 47 automated tests and a synthetic example; the registered analysis programs, whose SHA-256 values match those registered in OSF hyf36 (cohort A) and OSF 7jasg (cohort B); the exploratory programs with the dated plans of 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-17 and the record-level conformance checker; aggregate results for every table and figure; the deviation logs of both registrations; the 22-study literature evidence matrix; the cohort-B sampling frame and collection programs; and the generators of the supplement and the figures. Run python3 reproduce.py (Python 3.10 or later, numpy, matplotlib and git). It checks the registered hashes, runs the tests and the synthetic example, and regenerates the supplement tables and the figure data from the aggregate results. Before release, both levels passed on Python 3.10.12 with numpy 2.2.6 (Linux, aarch64) and on Python 3.13.16 with numpy 2.5.3 (Linux, x86_64), there also with every text output written with CRLF line endings. summary: Reproducibility package for the manuscript Coordinated Optimization of Microgrid Power Purchase and Energy Storage under Information-Temporal Constraints (Junjie Chen, Yu Liu, Ziyan Wang), submitted to Transactions on Energy Systems and Engineering Applications . The archive contains: (i) the solver and forecasting source code, including the entries that re-solve the whole evaluation period from the raw data files, export the per-slot quantities and re-check the evaluation period independently of the solver; (ii) the four case data files as released with the 2026 China Undergraduate Mathematical Contest in Modeling, Problem C; (iii) the daily result tables for the four information structures; and (iv) the verification outputs, comprising the pointwise physical verification over 192,384 strategy intervals, the independent cost back-calculation, the future-data and same-slot perturbation archives, and the strictly executable re-executions with their acceptance checks. Reproduction: unpack the archive and run the commands listed in README.txt from the archive root. Every script locates the archive root from its own position and uses no absolute path. A single structure takes about 15-20 minutes on one desktop core. Evaluation-period costs under the strictly executable protocol: 23.2305 million CNY (structure B, frozen day-ahead plan), 20.0279 (C, rolling adjustment), 24.5852 (D-B) and 20.5285 (D-C). The idealized-reference values reported alongside in the manuscript are 22.4599, 19.3188, 23.8493 and 19.8623 million CNY.

summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/23432006 . The paper (arXiv 2610.21914) is a pre-registered study of 465 merged agent-authored pull requests from 246 repositories (Sections 3.2-3.5). A frozen pipeline of four review agents and one fix agent ran every PR with three LLMs, and one mixed model per LLM tests CodeHealth against log total tokens (Sections 3.6-3.9). Each CodeHealth point goes with 3.5% to 6.1% lower token cost (Section 4.2, Table 8), but adding the size of the scored files absorbs the coefficient (Section 4.6.4, Table 15). I liked the handling of the pre-registration: the disclosure that review sessions started before filing, the amendment with a full re-collection of the 67 affected PRs (Section 3.12), and the file-size refit that weakens your own headline. I read it as a practitioner who runs coding agents every day. In my company the software development is done by AI agents, so maybe my practical side is useful here. Four comments. 1. On heavy tails (Sections 3.9, 4.2) - you note that one pilot PR was about 45% of a tier's mean token total, while in the main collection no PR exceeded 8.2% of a tier's token sum. In my measurement of 722 agent sessions (150,902 model calls, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22759216), about 3% of sessions gave 80% of the modeled cost. Sessions longer than 200 calls (8% of sessions) gave more than 90% of the money. So in my data the average is driven by a thin tail. What share of each LLM's tokens comes from the top 10% of PRs, and does the CodeHealth slope hold without them? 2. On cache and price (Section 3.8, Table 4, Section 6.3) - the outcome is input plus output tokens, with cached input recorded separately. In the same 722 sessions, more than 85% of the modeled cost was work with context (cache reads and cache writes). In a separate run of 168 sessions, 94.4% of billed tokens were re-reading context already sent (contextburn, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22712985). That is a share of tokens, not of the bill, because cached reads are the cheapest tokens. So a raw token total and a bill can rank PRs differently. Could you refit H1 with cached input priced at each provider's cache-read rate? 3. On paging long files (Sections 3.6, 5.2, 3.13) - the paper links the extra iterations to the 500-line limit per read call. In my guides I write that quality drops as the agent's context fills, and that heavy reading should go to a subagent so the main conversation stays clean. Since tool results are appended to the message history (Section 3.6), paging the median unhealthy-tier file of 2,146 lines puts every page into history that is re-sent on every later call. From the session records, can you count file-read calls and repeat reads of the same file per tier? That would test the paging explanation directly. 4. On the cost of what (Sections 5.5, 5.6, 6.3) - the study does not assess whether comments are correct or fixes are good. In my guides I write that every task needs its own check the agent can run. Without it, "looks done" is the only signal the agent has. I also use a second, fresh agent whose job is to refute the first one, because AI sounds equally sure when it is right and when it is wrong. For the 27-PR replication subsample (Section 3.11), you could run the repository tests after the fix and have a fresh agent try to refute each comment. Tokens per surviving finding would be a cheap first step toward Section 5.6. Thank you for a clear and useful paper. Competing interests Yes: the text cites the author's own technical reports (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22759216, 10.5281/zenodo.22712985); no connection to the article's authors. Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) The author declares that they used generative AI to come up with new ideas for their review.
title: PREreview of "CodeHealth Predicts the Token Cost of Agentic Code Review: A Pre-Registered Study of 465 Agent-Authored Pull Requests"

summary: Python code that reproduces all results, figures and supporting tables of Dixit, AchutaRao and Sandeep, "Future Warming Shortens the Memory of the Pacific Decadal Oscillation and Erodes a Source of Near-Term Predictability" (submitted to Earth's Future). summary: Background: Long-segment intramedullary cervical cord lesions can present a diagnostic challenge, particularly when imaging findings raise suspicion of an intramedullary neoplasm. Differentiating a syrinx from an intramedullary tumor is important for operative planning, as the surgical strategy may differ substantially. Case presentation: A 43-year-old female presented with a six-month history of progressive cervical pain with radicular symptoms, vertigo, left upper-limb sensory disturbance, and impaired left-hand grip. Neurological examination revealed preserved motor power of 5/5 in all four limbs, normal reflexes, and reduced functional grip in the left hand. MRI of the cervical spine demonstrated a long-segment expansile intramedullary lesion extending from the cervicomedullary junction to C7, without contrast enhancement. The radiological report also described Chiari malformation and syringomyelia. Given the diagnostic uncertainty and progressive symptoms, we performed urgent surgical exploration within two days of admission. We performed a C3–C7 laminoplasty to provide multilevel posterior access while preserving the laminar elements without instrumented fixation. Following durotomy and midline myelotomy, a syrinx was identified, with no obvious intramedullary tumor. Syringotomy and drainage were performed, and adjacent spinal cord tissue was obtained for biopsy. Graft duraplasty and reconstruction of the elevated laminae were completed. The patient had an uncomplicated postoperative course, with relief of pain and vertigo and resolution of sensory symptoms. She was discharged with intact motor power and improved but residual left-hand grip weakness. Follow-up MRI demonstrated cord decompression and drainage of the syrinx. Conclusion: This case illustrates the diagnostic uncertainty that may arise when a long-segment non-enhancing intramedullary cervical lesion is suspected to represent a tumor. Intraoperative findings guided the surgical procedure toward syringotomy and drainage, with tissue sampling to investigate a possible underlying neoplasm. Multilevel laminoplasty provided posterior access while allowing reconstruction of the cervical laminar elements. Histopathological confirmation and longer-term follow-up remain necessary.

title: Multilevel Cervical Laminoplasty and Syringotomy for a Long-Segment Cervical Syrinx Mimicking an Intramedullary Tumor: A Case Report

summary: This paper interprets black holes as information relay stations under global unitarity and fast scrambling. It connects holographic encoding, entanglement, Hayden–Preskill recovery, and Page-curve behaviour into a framework describing how infalling information is recorded and redistributed into radiation correlations. The central contribution is the separation of record and relay functions. Recording occurs on the scrambling timescale, while substantial recovery of information deposited before the Page time occurs near the Page transition. Unitary qubit models with up to fourteen black-hole qubits examine these connections using a mutual-information recovery proxy, revealing the role of early radiation and an approximately logistic recovery transition. Two model-specific predictions are proposed: gravitational-wave echoes spaced approximately by the scrambling time, conditional on a reflecting surface at a Planck-scale distance above the horizon; and a recovery transition whose rate remains of order one as system size increases, testable in quantum simulators. The contribution is a functional synthesis supported by model calculations. Keywords: black hole information paradox, holography, unitarity, Hayden–Preskill protocol, Page curve, information relay station, scrambling time, gravitational-wave echoes.
title: Black Holes as Information Relay Stations: A Six-Principle Synthesis from Holography to Unitarity

summary: EHR2Trace converts local hospital EHR extracts (delimited text and spreadsheets) into OMOP CDM 5.4 and MEDS. The two targets are derived independently from a single canonical layer rather than one from the other, every published row carries a link back to the source rows it came from, and fifty-five checks encode the properties a conversion must satisfy before it can be used as training data, including the leakage failures that are invisible to schema validation. Where the data does not answer a question, the converter blocks and says so instead of substituting a default. Companion paper: EHR2Trace: Auditable EHR Data Infrastructure for Patient World Models and Clinical Agents (arXiv:2609.38193).
title: EHR2Trace: a deterministic converter from local EHR exports to OMOP CDM 5.4 and MEDS, with row-level lineage

summary: Експертна методика визначає стадії та операції дослідження, однак сама їх послідовність іще не пояснює, за яких умов результатом однієї операції можна скористатися в наступній. У судовій гірничотехнічній експертизі найбільш відповідальними є переходи від відомостей, що їх містять матеріали, до реконструкції механізму події, від реконструкції – до оцінювання причинного значення обставин, а від установленої дії або бездіяльності – до її технічного співвіднесення з функціями конкретної особи. Мета роботи полягає у формуванні критеріїв, за якими придатність проміжного результату перевіряють до його застосування в наступній операції, та у з’ясуванні зв’язку між фактичною основою – сукупністю достатніх, узгоджених і простежуваних відомостей – і допустимими межами підсумкової відповіді експерта. Дослідження поєднало структурне моделювання, формально-логічний аналіз експертного міркування, зіставлення з положеннями судової експертології та теоретико-методичне узагальнення професійного досвіду у сфері судової гірничотехнічної експертизи. Застосування моделі проілюстровано на двох знеособлених типізованих ситуаціях із завершеної експертної практики 2015–2023 років, що відображають різний стан фактичної основи. Обґрунтовано поняття критерію контрольованого переходу й сім функціональних контрольних точок: відповідності питання компетенції експерта; достатності матеріалів; узгодженості та простежуваності відомостей; можливості реконструкції механізму; причинного значення обставин; суб’єктно-функціонального співвіднесення; синтезу й оцінювання результатів. Для фіксації методичного рішення запропоновано статуси контрольованого переходу: Т+ – дозволений перехід, Т± – обмежено дозволений перехід, Т– – недозволений перехід. Практичними результатами є модель проходження контрольної точки, матриця методичних рішень і структура робочої карти, придатні для використання як методичний модуль судової гірничотехнічної експертизи. Застосування критеріїв контрольованого переходу пов’язує стан фактичної основи з допустимим напрямом подальшого аналізу й запобігає формулюванню відповіді поза обумовленими межами.
title: Критерії контрольованого переходу між операціями судово-експертного дослідження як засіб забезпечення обґрунтованості висновку в судовій гірничотехнічній експертизі

Мета роботи полягає у формуванні критеріїв, за якими придатність проміжного результату перевіряють до його застосування в наступній операції, та у з’ясуванні зв’язку між фактичною основою – сукупністю достатніх, узгоджених і простежуваних відомостей – і допустимими межами підсумкової відповіді експерта. Дослідження поєднало структурне моделювання, формально-логічний аналіз експертного міркування, зіставлення з положеннями судової експертології та теоретико-методичне узагальнення професійного досвіду у сфері судової гірничотехнічної експертизи. Застосування моделі проілюстровано на двох знеособлених типізованих ситуаціях із завершеної експертної практики 2015–2023 років, що відображають різний стан фактичної основи. Обґрунтовано поняття критерію контрольованого переходу й сім функціональних контрольних точок: відповідності питання компетенції експерта; достатності матеріалів; узгодженості та простежуваності відомостей; можливості реконструкції механізму; причинного значення обставин; суб’єктно-функціонального співвіднесення; синтезу й оцінювання результатів. Для фіксації методичного рішення запропоновано статуси контрольованого переходу: Т+ – дозволений перехід, Т± – обмежено дозволений перехід, Т– – недозволений перехід. Практичними результатами є модель проходження контрольної точки, матриця методичних рішень і структура робочої карти, придатні для використання як методичний модуль судової гірничотехнічної експертизи. Застосування критеріїв контрольованого переходу пов’язує стан фактичної основи з допустимим напрямом подальшого аналізу й запобігає формулюванню відповіді поза обумовленими межами.
title: Критерії контрольованого переходу між операціями судово-експертного дослідження як засіб забезпечення обґрунтованості висновку в судовій гірничотехнічній експертизі

summary: Scripts, dated analysis plans, run logs, and deal-level estimates for a study of 38,991 completed acquisitions by listed or delisted acquirers across 37 countries, rumored between 2007 and 2025. Version 2.1 accompanies a manuscript under double anonymized peer review; author identification is withheld during the review. It changes no script, log, plan, or data file of version 2.0: it updates the title of the manuscript and renumbers the exhibits in the index (NUMBERS.md) to those of the manuscript as submitted (Tables 1 to 6; Online Appendix S1 to S22). Licensed return series and deal and firm data cannot be redistributed and are documented rather than included (LICENSE_AND_DATA.md). Start with README.md.
title: Replication package: Do acquisitions change systematic risk? Evidence on beta from 38,991 deals in 37 countries over 19 years

summary: Added Headline comparator configuration (Palomar follow-up item 5): a configuration naming the paper's main results, declared by lean-pkg formalization NAME --headline-config PATH ( --write records it), the registry field headline_config ( lean-pkg update NAME --headline-config PATH , '' clears) or the convention comparator.headline.json . Palomar's six keys only. formalization.yaml status.main_results then lists its theorems only, while the receipt and the gate keep binding the full comparison. Subset rule against the gate-bound comparator receipt validated at HEAD: every name covered (the --coverage rule) by a receipted configuration with the same Challenge and Solution modules, every definition hole signed in lean-pkg-signoff.json by such a configuration (the headline's own entry first; a main configuration's sign-off covers the same hole in the same modules); else refused, naming them. No receipt validating at HEAD: not applied, a warning, the old behaviour. palomar check runs the configuration checks on it and adds comparator.headline_uncovered (error) / comparator.headline_unjudged (warn), JSON headline ; palomar prepare bundles it under configs/ and README.txt names it for the main-results entry (Palomar: one configuration per submission). formalization --json gains headline . docs/comparator.md#headline-configuration-the-papers-main-results comparator host-check --routes [--json] : host and cluster planning before sbatch (field report #5). Per route ( judge : lake comparator in bwrap ; prepare : comparator-receipt --prepare ; transfer : build here, check the copied oleans with --verify-oleans , judge on a host that passes judge ), supported yes/no with the exact reason and the recommended command lines; executables resolved like type -P (the receipt slurm --template tool list read from the template), locale (a set locale that is not installed warns: the stderr warning a strict receipt refuses), ulimit -n and /proc/sys/fs/file-nr with the LEAN_NUM_THREADS=3 advice when tight, CPU affinity count and the cgroup v1/v2 memory limit. Additive JSON keys ( routes_schema host-routes/1 ); read-only, no network; never an unsandboxed route. comparator-receipt keeps earlier attempts. Before a run replaces an earlier run's stage files (it reruns the setup, or reruns the comparison after an earlier comparison, estimate or failure), it copies them to comparator-stages/attempts/NNN/ : stages.json , the stage logs, the olean manifest, the partial report and the per-unit files. The copy gets an attempt.json (schema comparator-attempt/1 : n , reason , commit , started_at , finished_at , failed_stage , verdict , olean_manifest_sha256 , and the sha256 of each kept file) and is made read-only. Before this, a rerun overwrote stages.json and cleared the logs of the failed run. Numbers are zero-padded and never reused ( attempts/NEXT survives a deleted attempt). lean-pkg never deletes an attempt or reads one back: resume, the slot cache and setup reuse read the current stage files, --from-prepared or --evidence-dir pointing into an attempt is refused, and receipts bind the current run only. A reused --prepare setup carries over without an attempt. stages.json gains started_at . comparator-receipt --attempts [DIR] [--json] lists the attempts read-only (exit 1 when a kept file changed or went missing). Nothing prunes attempts automatically; docs/comparator.md (Attempts) shows how to prune by hand. palomar port-modules NAME [--dry-run | --write] [--agent A] : the mechanical port of a package's tracked .lean files to Lean's module system, which Palomar requires. A dry run by default: from git objects at HEAD, a per-file report and a unified diff ( module first, after ordinary comments; import X to public import X , meta import to public meta import , never public import all ; the body in public section ... end , with no end when a scope stays open). Module-headed files are skipped, so a second run is a no-op; prelude files are refused with a reason

summary: Abstract : Background: The production of high-quality planting material during the nursery stage is essential for establishing productive, competitive, and sustainable oil palm plantations. Genetic material and container type may influence seedling development. Objective: To evaluate the growth of seedlings of two oil palm varieties, Deli × Compacta and Compacta × Ghana (Elaeis guineensis Jacq.), produced using two container types. Methods: The experiment was conducted in Macuspana, Tabasco, Mexico. Seedling growth was evaluated in two varieties, Deli × Compacta and Compacta × Ghana, using tube containers and plastic bags. A randomized complete block design was established with four treatments and four replications, with 100 seedlings per replication (400 seedlings per treatment; 1,600 seedlings in total). Plant height, number of leaves, and stipe diameter were measured every 15 days over 180 days. The same agronomic management was applied to all treatments. Descriptive statistics, analysis of variance (ANOVA), and Tukey’s multiple comparison test. Results: Significant differences among treatments were detected for the evaluated growth variables. For plant height, T3 (Compacta × Ghana in tube containers; CxGt) showed the greatest value at 180 days, reaching 68.37 ± 0.61 cm. For number of leaves, T1 (Deli × Compacta in tube containers; DxCt) and T3 (Compacta × Ghana in tube containers; CxGt) recorded 12.95 ± 0.11 and 12.38 ± 0.10 leaves, respectively, at 180 days. For stipe diameter, T1 and T2 showed the highest values at 180 days, with 2.21 ± 0.03 and 2.19 ± 0.03 cm, respectively, whereas T4 recorded 1.95 ± 0.02 cm. Conclusions: Under the conditions evaluated, seedlings produced in tube containers showed greater plant height and number of leaves at the end of the nursery period. Stipe diameter was higher in the Deli × Compacta material than in the Compacta × Ghana material at 180 days. These results support the potential use of tube containers for nursery production.

title: Growth of Seedlings of two Oil Palm Varieties (Elaeis guineensis Jacq.) in the Nursery Using two Container Types

summary: Background: Hyperlipidemia is a major risk factor for atherosclerosis and cardiovascular diseases. Evaluating drug utilization patterns provides critical insights into clinical practice and rational medicine use. Aim: To analyze the drug utilization patterns, clinical characteristics, and treatment outcomes among patients with hyperlipidemia in a hospital setting. Methodology: A retrospective observational study was conducted involving 150 hyperlipidemic patients receiving lipid-lowering pharmacotherapy at Visva Medical Centre and Hospital. Demographic data, prescribed treatment regimens, baseline, and post-treatment lipid profiles (Total Cholesterol, LDL, HDL, and Triglycerides) were collected and analyzed. Statistical significance was assessed using p-values. Results: Among the 150 participants, males constituted 53.33% (n=80) and females 46.67% (n=70). The majority of patients belonged to the 41–50 age group (n=42) and were classified as overweight based on BMI (n=65). Statin monotherapy was the predominant treatment choice. Atorvastatin was the most frequently prescribed agent (38.00%, n=57), followed by Rosuvastatin (26.67%, n=40), and Fenofibrate (20.00%, n=30). Combination therapy was prescribed in 15.34% (n=23) of patients. Post-treatment evaluation demonstrated statistically significant improvements across all lipid parameters (p < 0.001). Rosuvastatin monotherapy achieved the lowest current mean LDL level (114.35 mg/dL), Atorvastatin showed the highest mean HDL level (50.70 mg/dL), and Fenofibrate + Atorvastatin combination achieved the lowest triglyceride levels (161.60 mg/dL). Conclusion: Atorvastatin was the most commonly utilized lipid-lowering drug. All prescribed monotherapies and combination regimens resulted in statistically significant improvements in lipid profiles, demonstrating effective therapeutic outcomes in routine clinical practice.

title: AN ANALYSIS OF THE DRUG UTILIZATION PATTERNS OBSERVED IN PATIENTS WITH HYPERLIPIDEMIA

summary: Agentic frameworks, software libraries that coordinate large language model calls, tool use, memory, and multi step reasoning into autonomous or semi autonomous workflows, have moved from research prototypes to production infrastructure within a span of roughly two years. Four frameworks have emerged as leading options for enterprise adoption: LangGraph, a graph based orchestration library built around explicit state machines, CrewAI, a role based framework that models agents as a crew of collaborating specialists, Strands Agents, a model driven software development kit that emphasizes minimal orchestration code, and watsonx Orchestrate, a managed enterprise platform built around prepackaged skills and governance tooling. Despite rapid adoption, there has been little independent, head to head measurement of how these frameworks compare on the dimensions that matter most to enterprise adopters: end to end latency, latency under concurrent load, cost per task, reliability and error recovery, and enterprise readiness characteristics such as security, observability, and governance. This article presents an empirical benchmark of all four frameworks against a common task suite spanning six task categories and three complexity tiers. We report latency percentiles, a stage level latency breakdown, concurrency scaling behavior, cost per task, task success rates, and a structured enterprise readiness score. We further document each framework's orchestration topology, developer experience characteristics, and security and governance posture, and we translate the results into a practical decision framework for selecting among the four frameworks under different enterprise constraints. All benchmark figures in this article are illustrative, reflecting a representative test harness and reference workload rather than any single vendor's published numbers, and are intended to demonstrate a repeatable evaluation method rather than a definitive ranking.
title: LANGGRAPH, CREWAI, STRANDS, OR WATSONX ORCHESTRATE? AN EMPIRICAL BENCHMARK OF AGENTIC FRAMEWORKS FOR ENTERPRISE READINESS AND LATENCY

summary: This repository provides the Python implementation of a self-supervised hybrid deep learning framework for lung CT image classification. The pipeline includes CT image preprocessing, SimCLR-based self-supervised learning, VGG16 and Swin Transformer feature extraction, attention-based feature fusion, PCA-based dimensionality reduction, and classification using XGBoost, Random Forest, and MLP. The repository also includes dataset preparation scripts, baseline comparisons, ablation experiments, evaluation metrics, explainable AI methods, configuration files, and implementation documentation. The framework is designed for binary classification of benign and malignant lung nodules using LIDC-IDRI and IQ-OTH/NCCD CT datasets.

summary: Chlorine-based disinfectants are standard for environmental-surface disinfection in healthcare facilities, yet their reaction with organic residues generates disinfection by-products (DBPs) whose occurrence, levels, and occupational relevance on hospital surfaces remain uncharacterized. Key gaps are the lack of a validated method and baseline data, the unresolved origin of surface N-nitrosamines, and the unknown influence of chlorine, temperature, humidity, and pre-cleaning on the surface DBP signal. We developed an isotope-dilution wipe-sampling, solid-phase extraction, and ultra-performance liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) method for eight priority DBPs, applied it to 125 wipe samples from five departments across three campuses of a tertiary hospital in Wenzhou, and complemented field work with stainless-steel coupon experiments. Validation gave r ≥ 0.999, detection limits of 0.8–3.8 pg/cm², and recoveries of 78.4%–96.8%; field detection and quantification frequencies were 87.2% (95% CI 80.2–92.0%) and 69.6% (95% CI 61.1–77.0%), with operating rooms showing the highest total load (Kruskal–Wallis H(4) = 27.86, P < 0.001) though no pairwise contrast survived Bonferroni correction. In coupon experiments the net signal rose with chlorine and temperature but not humidity, with an unexplained chlorine-dependent increment (≈55% at 2000 mg/L) reflecting analytical signal behavior rather than verified formation chemistry, and pre-cleaning reduced haloacetic acids and chlorophenols by 35–55% but N-nitrosamines by only 3–9%. These results provide the first isotope-dilution baseline of DBP loads on healthcare surfaces, a reproducible monitoring method, and occurrence data for revising disinfection and occupational-hygiene standards, and they identify precursor-controlled formation experiments, biological monitoring, and direct testing of medical rubber as next steps.

summary: Data Type: CSV, Experiment  Organized by: Research group of Shenzhen Research Institute, University of International Business and Economics, and a principal researcher from the University of Sassari, Italy  Approval ID: UIBE-4635876 The dataset contains 876 linked scene records representing 73 participants, each contributing responses to 12 virtual tourism presentations. Six destination settings are represented: a heritage courtyard, coastal promenade, forest trail, museum gallery, mountain lookout and historic street. Each setting has a LiDAR and a photogrammetric version, yielding 438 records per reconstruction condition. Each row identifies a participant, destination and reconstruction condition. The source CSV contains participant age and VR familiarity, presentation order, exposure duration, experiential ratings and technical descriptors. Experiential variables include psychological immersion, presence, perceived spatial coherence, emotional valence, arousal and workload. Technical variables include geometric error, texture ratings, frame rate, motion summaries and the interval between modality sessions. Neural features comprise 1,200 EEG values organised across 30 channels and 40 frequency bins spanning 1–40 Hz, together with 12 fMRI regional summaries. The regional labels cover bilateral dorsolateral prefrontal, precentral, postcentral, inferior parietal and superior parietal regions, plus ventromedial prefrontal cortex and precuneus. These values use arbitrary units and do not represent raw electrical waveforms or anatomically extracted BOLD measurements. The analysis CSV aggregates EEG frequency values into five bands: delta, theta, alpha, beta and gamma. This produces 150 EEG features per record. Combining these with the 12 regional summaries produces 162 neural predictors. Mean immersion combines the two session ratings; values of at least 4.5 define the high immersion category. The analysis file also contains participant validation fold assignments, held-out predictions and classifier scores. All records from a participant share the same validation fold. Prediction and score columns are analytical outputs and must be excluded from model inputs. Mean immersion is 4.59 for LiDAR and 3.95 for photogrammetry. Verified primary balanced accuracy is 81.97% for EEG, 79.66% for fMRI and 79.01% for the combined model.
title: Decoding Immersive VR Tourism: Reconstruction Quality and Neural Indicators of Immersion

summary: R scripts and aggregate tables that reproduce every number, table and figure in the article What a national health information system measures: a cross-sectional analysis of respiratory syncytial virus records in Bulgaria, 2022–2026 (Folia Medica, manuscript 215603) and its supplementary files. The package contains the reconstruction ledger of the Ministry of Health release of Bulgarian National Health Information System (NHIS) records for ICD-10 J21.0, J12.1, J20.5 and B97.4; exclusion and validation counts; the 110 distinct laboratory result values (109 text strings and the empty text field of numeric results) with their assigned RSV class and the rule that fired; a script that rebuilds the hospitalisation episodes from the released worksheet; annual population denominators at national and district level (National Statistical Institute table 206/649, population on 31 December 2022–2025); the aggregate model input (year × age × sex cases and person-years, with and without Sliven); model output and diagnostics; and the article figures. Aggregate data only. No record-level rows, identifiers or dates of birth are included; the record-level extract can be requested from the Bulgarian Ministry of Health under the Access to Public Information Act. See README.md for the file map, data sources, disclosure control and how to re-run the pipeline. Tables and figures: CC BY 4.0; R scripts: MIT licence.

summary: English abstract Can an artificial agent have subjective experience while lacking unrestricted authority to replace its governing task objective? This paper treats that possibility as a distinct design and evaluation problem, termed the third case. It separates phenomenal consciousness, goal-directed behavior, operational competence, temporal continuity, and decision authority. The hypothetical case, a functionally testable candidate, and the evidence concerning experience are different descriptions. The prompt-issuer is an explicit role that may itself be occupied by a potentially experiencing executor under upstream constraints. The framework preserves the project-specific composition B-Core = A-Core ⊕ Purple Box/Present. A-Core denotes a potentially stateful, learning, multi-model cognitive and executive system; Purple is an undisclosed candidate addition with intended history-dependent causal effects. ESSENTIAL is a protected specification of constraints and revision authority, logically associated with A-Core. A targeted comparison with IDA, LIDA, adjustable autonomy, and existing agent controls, at the access levels stated in section 2.4, locates the proposal within established work. The contribution is a project-specific evaluation contract for externally governed, internally continuous execution, rather than a demonstrated new consciousness mechanism. Three limited analytical observations concern goal delegation, policy differences masked by a shared guard, and the gap between an architectural effect and consciousness. The proposed studies distinguish causal relevance from practical benefit, score feasible completion and justified infeasibility separately, and control initialization, history transfer, order, and dependent observations. No empirical result or proof of phenomenal consciousness is claimed. Functional findings could remain valuable if the consciousness hypothesis is rejected; credible welfare concerns would require assessment that task success alone cannot resolve. Magyar absztrakt Lehet-e egy mesterséges ágensnek szubjektív átélése úgy, hogy közben nincs korlátlan jogköre irányadó feladatcéljának lecserélésére? A tanulmány ezt a lehetőséget önálló tervezési és értékelési problémaként kezeli, és harmadik esetnek nevezi. Elkülöníti a fenomenális tudatosságot, a célirányos viselkedést, a működési kompetenciát, az időbeli folytonosságot és a döntési jogkört. A hipotetikus eset, a funkcionálisan vizsgálható jelölt és az átélésre vonatkozó bizonyíték eltérő leírások. A promptot kiadó szereplő kifejezetten meghatározott szerepet tölt be, amelyet maga is betölthet egy esetleg átéléssel rendelkező, a hierarchia felsőbb szintjéről korlátozott végrehajtó. A keretrendszer megőrzi a projektre jellemző B-Core = A-Core ⊕ Purple Box/Present összetételt. Az A-Core egy potenciálisan állapotos, tanuló, több modellt használó kognitív és végrehajtó rendszert jelöl; a Purple egy nem közölt felépítésű kiegészítőjelölt, amelynek előzményfüggő oksági hatásokat szánnak. Az ESSENTIAL a korlátok és a módosítási jogkör védett specifikációja, amely logikailag az A-Core-hoz kapcsolódik. Az IDA-val, a LIDA-val, az állítható autonómiával és az ágensek meglévő irány&i
title: The Third Case: Prompt-Governed Agency under a Consciousness Hypothesis
