summary: The spoof speech detection (SSD) is the essential countermeasure for automatic speaker verification systems. Although SSD with magnitude features in the frequency domain has shown promising results, the phase information also can be important to capture the artefacts of certain types of spoofing attacks. Thus, both magnitude and phase features must be considered to ensure the generalization ability to diverse types of spoofing attacks. In this paper, we investigate the failure reason of feature-level fusion of the previous works through the entropy analysis from which we found that the randomness difference between magnitude and phase features is large, which can interrupt the feature-level fusion via backend neural network; thus, we propose a phase network to reduce that difference. Our SSD system: phase network equipped Res2Net achieved significant performance improvement, specifically in the spoofing attack for which the phase information is considered to be important. Also, we demonstrate our SSD system in both known- and unknown-kind SSD scenarios for practical applications.
title: Phase-Aware Spoof Speech Detection Based on Res2Net with Phase Network

summary: Automatic speaker verification (ASV) systems are highly vulnerable to presentation attacks, also called spoofing attacks. Replay is among the simplest attacks to mount - yet difficult to detect reliably. The generalization failure of spoofing countermeasures (CMs) has driven the community to study various alternative deep learning CMs. The majority of them are supervised approaches that learn a human-spoof discriminator. In this paper, we advocate a different, deep generative approach that leverages from powerful unsupervised manifold learning in classification. The potential benefits include the possibility to sample new data, and to obtain insights to the latent features of genuine and spoofed speech. To this end, we propose to use variational autoencoders (VAEs) as an alternative backend for replay attack detection, via three alternative models that differ in their class-conditioning. The first one, similar to the use of Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) in spoof detection, is to train independently two VAEs - one for each class. The second one is to train a single conditional model (C-VAE) by injecting a one-hot class label vector to the encoder and decoder networks. Our final proposal integrates an auxiliary classifier to guide the learning of the latent space. Our experimental results using constant-Q cepstral coefficient (CQCC) features on the ASVspoof 2017 and 2019 physical access subtask datasets indicate that the C-VAE offers substantial improvement in comparison to training two separate VAEs for each class. On the 2019 dataset, the C-VAE outperforms the VAE and the baseline GMM by an absolute 9 - 10% in both equal error rate (EER) and tandem detection cost function (t-DCF) metrics. Finally, we propose VAE residuals - the absolute difference of the original input and the reconstruction as features for spoofing detection.
title: Deep Generative Variational Autoencoding for Replay Spoof Detection in Automatic Speaker Verification

summary: Automatic speaker verification (ASV) systems are highly vulnerable to presentation attacks, also called spoofing attacks. Replay is among the simplest attacks to mount - yet difficult to detect reliably. The generalization failure of spoofing countermeasures (CMs) has driven the community to study various alternative deep learning CMs. The majority of them are supervised approaches that learn a human-spoof discriminator. In this paper, we advocate a different, deep generative approach that leverages from powerful unsupervised manifold learning in classification. The potential benefits include the possibility to sample new data, and to obtain insights to the latent features of genuine and spoofed speech. To this end, we propose to use variational autoencoders (VAEs) as an alternative backend for replay attack detection, via three alternative models that differ in their class-conditioning. The first one, similar to the use of Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) in spoof detection, is to train independently two VAEs - one for each class. The second one is to train a single conditional model (C-VAE) by injecting a one-hot class label vector to the encoder and decoder networks. Our final proposal integrates an auxiliary classifier to guide the learning of the latent space. Our experimental results using constant-Q cepstral coefficient (CQCC) features on the ASVspoof 2017 and 2019 physical access subtask datasets indicate that the C-VAE offers substantial improvement in comparison to training two separate VAEs for each class. On the 2019 dataset, the C-VAE outperforms the VAE and the baseline GMM by an absolute 9 - 10% in both equal error rate (EER) and tandem detection cost function (t-DCF) metrics. title: Deep Generative Variational Autoencoding for Replay Spoof Detection in Automatic Speaker Verification

summary: Speaker verification (SV) performance degrades under language mismatch due to the entanglement of speaker identity with language-specific acoustic cues. To address this problem, we leverage large-scale self-supervised pre-trained models (PTMs) to learn language-agnostic speaker representations. We utilize PTMs as robust front-end feature extractors, capitalizing on their rich acoustic and linguistic knowledge acquired from vast, diverse audio data. These generalized features are then used to train a downstream speaker embedding network, effectively disentangling speaker identity from language-specific characteristics. We validate our approach on the TidyVoice2026 benchmark, which benchmarks SV under language mismatch. Our proposed system (team T02) achieves equal error rates (EERs) of 2.21% on tv26_eval-A and 2.99% on tv26_eval-U.
title: Cross-Lingual Speaker Verification with Self-Supervised Pre-Trained Models

summary: Embedding enhancement improves speaker verification under acoustic mismatch without modifying a frozen backbone. Recent work has established a practical label-free setting for this task, but often adopts increasingly structured formulations. Here, the clean target is directly observed during training, making enhancement a matching problem on the unit hypersphere. We model the clean target with a von Mises--Fisher (vMF) likelihood and profile out a sample-wise concentration parameter, yielding a simple closed-form objective with adaptive weighting. Across VoxCeleb1, VoxSRC23, CN-Celeb, VOiCES, and VC-Mix, the proposed method largely preserves the baseline and gives clearer gains on challenging mismatch sets. It also remains stable under a broad single-view recipe, where a recent diffusion baseline becomes less reliable in controlled comparisons. These results suggest that effective label-free embedding enhancement in this setting does not require a highly structured formulation.
title: Revisiting Label-Free Speaker Embedding Enhancement with vMF Profile Likelihood

summary: Speech-pretrained models have shown promise in animal bioacoustics, but the factors governing their cross-species transfer remain poorly understood. We evaluate 15 frozen encoders spanning monolingual and multilingual speech, speaker verification, animal bioacoustics, and general audio on caller identification across four species and call-type classification across three. Differences between the strongest speech- and animal-pretrained representations range from $-0.027$ to $+0.119$ UAR; speech is significantly better in three of seven settings ($p<0.01$) and not significantly different in the remaining four. Controlled comparisons show no systematic advantage from increased language coverage or animal-domain pretraining, while frozen speaker-verification embeddings transfer poorly. The results also show that transfer is strongly layer-dependent: raw-waveform models peak early, whereas patch-spectrogram models peak deeper.
title: Neural Representations, Natural Connections: What Transfers From Human Speech Foundation Models to Animal Vocalizations?

summary: C. J Tully. Independent Research https://orcid.org/0009-0007-5661-7332 chloetully5@gmail.com   18 th October 2026                   Most of what you call your life arrives half a second late. Something happens. A sound, a face, a tightness in the chest. Before you have chosen anything, a voice — yours, apparently — has already named it, judged it, and filed it under a chapter called me. You do not notice the filing. You notice the file. And so you spend your days inside a commentary about a world you have not, strictly speaking, met. This is not a moral failure. It is a timing error. Awareness is not a mood you work up and not a belief you adopt. It is what is already underway before the sentence starts. The breath you are taking does not consult your biography. The light on the wall does not ask what you meant to become. For a fraction of a second there is contact without a commentator. Then the commentator returns, a little late, a little proud, and explains what just occurred as if the explanation were the event. People talk about waking up as if it were a prize for the patient and the pure. It is closer to catching a clerical mistake. You have been treating the report as the room. The report is useful. It gets you across streets, through grief, into love, out of traffic. It is also not the thing it reports on. The word water has never once made a hand wet. Watch the exact moment a thought claims you. There is a sensation, then a grab. The grab feels like identity. It is older than that, and thinner. It is a habit of ownership so practiced it forgot it was optional. You do not have to defeat it. You only have to notice that noticing is already happening, and that the one who seems to be doing the noticing cannot be found as an object inside what is noticed. Sit with that past the point of comfort. Comfort is how the narration gets rehired. If the “you” who plans, defends, remembers, and suffers is a pattern appearing in awareness, then who has been afraid all this time? Not a cosmic answer. A local one. Look. Fear is weather. The sky it crosses was not manufactured by the storm. Nothing theatrical follows from this. You will still want things. You will still lose them. You will still answer the message and miss the person. The only change is a small, stubborn order of operations: experience first, story second. And the recognition, quiet enough to miss if you perform it, that you were never inside the story. You were the place it was being told. That place does not improve. It does not arrive. It does not need you to become someone else in order to be what it already is. The only work, if it can even be called work, is to stop leaving a half-second early — to remain, once, with what is here before you agree with your own explanation of it. Stay. The explanation can wait. It always could.
title: Most of what you call your life arrives half a second late.

summary: The Empty Occupant: Answerability, Testimony, and the Limits of Machine-Mediated Authority examines a problem of institutional AI: automated decisions can scale faster than institutions' capacity to justify, reconsider, correct, or repair them. Identifying a responsible institution does not establish that its decisions were warrantedly adopted or that resulting obligations can be discharged. Across philosophy of language, social epistemology, social ontology, normative theory, AI governance, and administrative law , the monograph develops a substrate-neutral Discursive Ontology connecting three questions: who bears an institutional commitment, what warrants its adoption, and whether answerability can be sustained at scale. It distinguishes commitment ownership, warranted adoption, adequate discharge, causal contribution, and legal liability. Five contributions follow: Discursive Ontology and Answerability. Defines commitment-bearing through four jointly necessary relations within reciprocal normative standing: attribution continuity, challenge-responsive reconsideration, repair competence, and standing-consequence . It distinguishes Actual, Residual, Prospective, and Empty Occupancy . Empty Occupancy requires presentation as an independent bearer and affirmative evidence that the relevant standing is absent , not a mere machine interface. The axiom is that missing bearership is not defective ownership : a principal may remain responsible for commitments its interface cannot independently bear. Testimony Without a Testifier. Separates hearer-side epistemic uptake from speaker-side commitment ownership . Machine outputs can inform without establishing an answerable speaker. On assurance-based accounts, they can exercise testimonial force without constituting testimony . Reliability, fluency, and conversational memory alone confer no authority to retract a commitment. Normative Sponsorship. Specifies five conditions for warranted institutional adoption: epistemic access, authority, review bandwidth, independent rejection, and repair power . Its contestation-grain opacity threshold requires reconstructing relevant grounds where a challenge must take effect—at input, case, rule, shared-premise, or architecture—without complete transparency. It distinguishes technical opacity from organizational capture , where reasons are knowable but cannot bind, and considers model succession and agentic chains. Deontic Debt and Institutional Insolvency. Derives consequence-sensitive reconsideration from the defeasibility of presumptive authority. Deontic Debt comprises matured obligations deficiently serviced, not simply pending work. Institutional Insolvency arises when no credible service plan meets relevant obligations and protections for a specified claim mix, issuance scale, lawful architecture, and horizon. Its consequence is targeted loss of presumptive authority , not automatic legal invalidity or release from ownership and repair duties. Institutional Stewardship. Connects permissible automated use to warranted sponsorship, protective review, binding reconsideration, and effective repair. Restoration requires legacy discharge, demonstrable future capacity, and scaled resumption. Public-record analyses examine Australia's Robodebt scheme, Moffatt v. Air Canada , A.M.C. v. Smith (TennCare), the Post Office Horizon scandal, the Dutch childcare-benefits affair, and a press-based DPD generative-interface episode. Neither Air Canada nor DPD establishes determinate Empty Occupancy. An explicitly fictional, stipulated Meridian–Aster appeals-agent comparator yields a determinate verdict: Aster lacks independent standing while its insurer, Meridian, remains the Actual institutional bearer. This is not empirical evidence and settles neither sponsorship nor serviceability. A stipulated positive comparator illustrates review and repair. Objections address synthetic agency, status conferral, intentionality, human–machine parit
title: The Empty Occupant: Answerability, Testimony, and the Limits of Machine-Mediated Authority

summary: We develop a rigorous finite-dimensional mathematical framework connecting the renormalization group, gradient flows, Lyapunov stability, and noncooperative game theory. The central object is a renormalization-group flow written in gradient form, dg_i/dt = β_i(g) = - ∑_j G_ij(g) ∂Γ/∂g_j(g),          (1) where g = (g_1, …, g_n) belongs to an open domain M ⊂ ℝⁿ, Γ is a C² function, and G(g) is a symmetric positive-definite matrix. We associate to this flow a common-payoff game whose payoff is U(g) = - Γ(g).                   (2) We prove, with complete arguments, that ordinary Nash equilibria always imply renormalization-group fixed points, but the converse is false. We then identify the exact condition under which a fixed point becomes a genuine stable equilibrium of the game: a nondegenerate renormalization-group fixed point is asymptotically stable if and only if the Hessian of Γ is positive definite, if and only if it is a strict local minimum of Γ, if and only if it is a strict strong Nash equilibrium of U = -Γ. The distinction between ordinary Nash equilibrium and strong Nash equilibrium is essential. Ordinary Nash equilibria allow only unilateral deviations, while strong Nash equilibria exclude all small joint deviations. We provide explicit counterexamples showing that fixed points need not be Nash equilibria, that ordinary Nash equilibria need not be stable, and that invertibility of G alone does not imply finiteness of equilibria. We also prove global existence results under compactness and finiteness results under Morse nondegeneracy. The paper is self-contained at the level of multivariable calculus, linear algebra, ordinary differential equations, and basic Lyapunov stability theory. The framework is intentionally conditional: it does not claim that the gradient-flow representation has been proven in four-dimensional QCD or in any specific quantum field theory. Those issues are placed in a final section of open problems.
title: Gradient-Flow Renormalization Group as a Common-Potential Game: A Rigorous Equivalence Between Asymptotically Stable Fixed Points and Strict Strong Nash Equilibria

summary: We develop a rigorous reduction inside the Connes–Consani–Moscovici programme for the Riemann hypothesis. The main unconditional result is the following symmetry principle: for the truncated Weil quadratic form QW_λ^N, simplicity of the lowest eigenvalue ε_N implies evenness of the corresponding ground state ξ, provided the natural reflection symmetry γV_n = V_{-n} and the normalization ℓ_N(ξ) = 1 are imposed. This converts two structural requirements of the programme into one spectral requirement. We then prove a precise spectral approximation criterion. If the finite-dimensional form QW_λ^N approximates the prolate wave operator PW_λ in a form-strong sense sufficient to preserve the first isolated simple eigenvalue, then ε_N is simple for all large N. Combining this criterion with the symmetry principle gives evenness of the ground state. Finally, we prove a windowed determinant criterion for the Riemann hypothesis. If the regularized determinants attached to the Connes–Consani–Moscovici finite-rank perturbations have only real zeros and converge locally uniformly, on an exhausting family of windows, to nonzero multiples of the Riemann Ξ-function, then every zero of Ξ is real, and therefore the Riemann hypothesis follows. The paper separates cleanly the proved logical reductions from the analytic objectives required for their unconditional verification. Those objectives are collected in a final section of open problems, giving a foundational reference for the remaining work in the programme. We emphasize that this paper does not claim an unconditional proof of the Riemann hypothesis; rather, it provides a precise structural reduction and isolates the remaining analytic challenges.
title: Evenness from Simplicity in the Truncated Weil Quadratic Form and Conditional Spectral Criteria for the Riemann Hypothesis

summary: International business (IB) theory explains how firms enter foreign markets, allocate ownership, govern cross-border activities, build networks, and accumulate market knowledge. Less explicit attention has been given to the internationalization of the firm’s continuing operating system itself. This article develops the concept of operational internationalization: the cross-border extension of recurring fulfilment, inventory, logistics, service, compliance, and information processes, regardless of whether the underlying capabilities are fully owned by the focal firm. It further introduces operational embeddedness and boundary asymmetry to explain why ownership, governance, operational, and jurisdictional boundaries may overlap without expanding synchronously. Sovereign jurisdiction is treated as a constitutive boundary because tax, customs, data, product, environmental, and related rules shape which cross-border configurations are institutionally admissible. The framework becomes dynamic through reverse value-information flow, whereby economically consequential market and jurisdictional information generated abroad enters subsequent production, allocation, service, and organizational decisions. Just-in-Place (JIP) is positioned within this architecture as the enactment logic through which geographically and institutionally dispersed capabilities are selectively activated and recombined. A comparative public-disclosure analysis of Linamar and JD Logistics provides complementary evidence of inward informational feedback and outward operational extension. The article reconceptualizes internationalization as a reflexive, multi-boundary process in which the operating system itself becomes an analytically distinct object of cross-border expansion.
title: Internationalizing the Operating System: Operational Embeddedness, Jurisdictional Boundaries, and Just-in-Place

summary: No contexto atual de valorização das práticas sustentáveis e da eficiência operacional, a logística reversa apresenta-se como uma ferramenta estratégica na gestão de resíduos sólidos em ambientes aeroportuários. O presente estudo tem como objetivo analisar os principais desafios relacionados à logística reversa no Aeroporto Internacional de São Paulo/Guarulhos, bem como avaliar o uso de tecnologias aplicadas à logística como forma de otimização dos processos. A metodologia adotada baseia-se em revisão bibliográfica e análise de estudos de caso. Os resultados demonstram que a ausência de um sistema integrado de gestão de resíduos, aliada à baixa utilização de tecnologias, compromete a eficiência operacional e gera perdas financeiras. Como proposta, sugere-se a implantação de um sistema inteligente de monitoramento de resíduos com uso de Internet das Coisas (IoT), visando aumentar a eficiência da coleta seletiva e o reaproveitamento de materiais.
title: Logística Reversa e Tecnologia Aplicada no Aeroporto Internacional de Guarulhos: Desafios e Soluções Operacionais

summary: We study diagonal infinite-order operators on the flat torus of the form P = A(|D|),                        (1) where D = -i∇ is the momentum operator on T^n and A: [0,∞) → (0,∞) is a positive radial symbol with super-polynomial growth. Under explicit log-convexity and steepness assumptions on A, we prove a Weyl law for the eigenvalue counting function, a leading heat-kernel asymptotic, and the small positive-s behavior of the spectral zeta function. The main proved results are the following. 1. Weyl law with an elementary remainder: N_P(λ) = C_n (A^(-1)(λ))^n + O((A^(-1)(λ))^(n-1)), λ → ∞,                                 (2) where C_n = ω_n/(2π)^n, ω_n = π^(n/2)/Γ(n/2 + 1).           (3) 2. Leading heat-kernel asymptotic: Tr(e^(-tP)) = C_n (R(t))^n (1 + o(1)), t → 0+,           (4) where R(t) is defined by A(R(t)) = 1/t.                    (5) 3. Zeta asymptotics in terms of the inverse growth function. Define G(u) = (A^(-1)(e^u))^n.  (6) Assume that, as u → ∞, G(u) ~ u^ρ L(u), where ρ ≥ 0 and L is slowly varying. If ρ = 0, assume also that G(u) → ∞. Then, as s → 0+, ζ_P(s) ~ C_n Γ(ρ + 1) s^(-ρ) L(1/s). 4. For the model symbols A(r) = exp(l r^q), l > 0, q ≥ 1,                                       (7) and, more generally, A(r) = exp^(k)(l r^q), k ≥ 2, l > 0, q > 0, we obtain explicit asymptotics. If d = n/q, then:                                  (8) For depth k = 1:               (9) N_P(λ) ~ C_n l^(-d) (log λ)^d, Tr(e^(-tP)) ~ C_n l^(-d) (log(1/t))^d, ζ_P(s) ~ C_n l^(-d) Γ(d + 1) s^(-d). For depth k ≥ 2: N_P(λ) ~ C_n l^(-d) (log^(k) λ)^d, Tr(e^(-tP)) ~ C_n l^(-d) (log^(k)(1/t))^d, ζ_P(s) ~ C_n l^(-d) (log^(k-1)(1/s))^d. Here exp^(1)(x) = e^x, exp^(k+1)(x) = exp(exp^(k)(x)), log^(1)(x) = log x, and log^(k+1)(x) = log(log^(k)(x)). The paper proves only statements that are fully justified in the diagonal commutative model. Noncommutative residue theory, decomposition assumptions, spectral triples, local residue pairing formulas, integrality statements, and topological residue theorems are not proved here and are listed as open problems.
title: HEAT KERNEL, WEYL LAW, AND ZETA ASYMPTOTICS FOR DIAGONAL INFINITE-ORDER OPERATORS WITH SUPER-POLYNOMIAL GROWTH

summary: Code, trained weights and campaign results for the paper "Morphological diffusion by ball births: generative models of binary images with exact Betti increments" by M. Zéraï, submitted to the Journal of Mathematical Imaging and Vision. The model generates binary images by births of maximal balls. Its forward process is a random granulometry, and its reverse process learns a birth map. morpho_repro.tar.gz contains the implementation (model, sampler, exact Euler increments, measurement protocol), the averaged (EMA) weights of all trained models on the three datasets (GRF, BBBC039 nuclei masks, MNIST), the campaign reports and logs, and the GRF data. README.md gives the hyperparameters, the source of each table and the reproduction commands. figs_print.tar.gz contains the figure boards of the paper with their statistics. The BBBC039 masks and MNIST are public and are downloaded by prepare_data.sh. Note: the two archives are gzip-compressed tar files, deposited as morpho_repro.tar and figs_print.tar (README.md names them morpho_repro.tar.gz and figs_print.tar.gz). Extract them with: tar xzf morpho_repro.tar
title: Morphological diffusion by ball births: code, trained weights and campaign results

summary: Region means and contrasts with a full error budget, correlated shift errors, error bars for shot noise, a faster fit_map , two tutorials, and three fixes. Added region_mean(coefficients, dw1, dw2, sigma1, sigma2, mask, *, shift_correlation=None, ref_sigma=None) and region_contrast(coefficients, dw1, dw2, sigma1, sigma2, mask_a, mask_b, *, shift_correlation=None) , returning a RegionEstimate : the mean strain and density of a map region, or region A minus region B, with the error split into shift noise (averages down over pixels), calibration (from a two-mode CalibrationResult ; does not average down) and reference frequencies ( ref_sigma ; does not average down, and cancels exactly in a contrast). region_mean also tests whether the pixels agree within their error bars (chi-square with 2 (N - 1) degrees of freedom, the same in shift space and in (strain, density) space) and reports the pixel spread. Validated against the mean and per-pixel covariances of SeparationModel.invert , separation_with_calibration , finite differences of a re-solve, and seeded Monte Carlo over 400 trials that repeat the calibration, the map noise and the reference error (spread within 12 % of the reported error bars). Propagation as in JCGM 100:2008 (GUM), 5.2.2, Eq. (13). SeparationModel.invert(..., shift_correlation=None) : the correlation of the two shift errors (from a joint fit) enters the error bars through the full 2 x 2 shift covariance. Zero gives the old result bit for bit. On 400 repeats of two overlapping E' + A'1 peaks the density error bar without the correlation is 27 % above the actual spread; with it, it matches (tutorial 2). separation_with_calibration passes it through. MapFitResult.shift_correlation : the correlation of the two shift errors per pixel (the joint fit's value, 0 for separate window fits, NaN where masked). noise="varying" in fit_lorentzian , fit_two_modes and fit_map : error bars from the heteroskedasticity-consistent ("sandwich") covariance of H. White, Econometrica 48, 817 (1980), for spectra whose noise level changes along the axis, as shot noise does. Fitted values are unchanged. On 600 seeded Poisson spectra the center scatter is 1.7 times the default error bar and within 10 % of the new one; checked also against an independent finite-difference sandwich (relative 1e-5). The default, noise="constant" , is unchanged. README example 18 (shot noise) and a "Tutorials" section. Fixed calibrate_lever_arms , plan_calibration and design_references judged identifiability from the raw singular values of the design, which depends on the units. Before: the six-state design of the tests with the density in cm^-2 raised ValueError: reference states are collinear ... ( plan_calibration returned identifiable=False ). After: it gives the arms of the fit in 1e13 cm^-2, rescaled (A'1 density arm -2.2798e-13 per cm^-2 against -2.2798 per 1e13 cm^-2; relative 1e-10). The test is now made on the design with unit-length columns (also with fit_offset=True ). Test: test_calibration_does_not_depend_on_the_density_unit , test_planning_does_not_depend_on_the_density_unit . bayesian_map_inversion(..., fill_masked=True) : the same unit dependence in its pooled-information check. Added region_mean(coefficients, dw1, dw2, sigma1, sigma2, mask, *, shift_correlation=None, ref_sigma=None) and region_contrast(coefficients, dw1, dw2, sigma1, sigma2, mask_a, mask_b, *, shift_correlation=None) , returning a RegionEstimate : the mean strain and density of a map region, or region A minus region B, with the error split into shift noise (averages down over pixels), calibration (from a two-mode CalibrationResult ; does not average down) and reference frequencies ( ref_sigma ; does not average down, and cancels exactly in a contrast). region_mean also tests whether the pixels agree within their error bars (chi-square with 2 (N - 1) degrees of freedom, the same in shift space and in (strain, density) space) and reports the pixel spread. Validated against the mean and per-pixel covariances of SeparationModel.invert , separation_with_calibration , finite differences of a re-solve, and seeded Monte Carlo over 400 trials that repeat the calibration, the map noise and the reference error (spread within 12 % of the reported error bars). Propagation as in JCGM 100:2008 (GUM), 5.2.2, Eq. (13). SeparationModel.invert(..., shift_correlation=None) : the correlation of the two shift errors (from a joint fit) enters the error bars through the full 2 x 2 shift covariance. Zero gives the old result bit for bit. On 400 repeats of two overlapping E' + A'1 peaks the density error bar without the correlation is 27 % above the actual spread; with it, it matches (tutorial 2). separation_with_calibration passes it through. MapFitResult.shift_correlation : the correlation of the two shift errors per pixel (the joint fit's value, 0 for separate window fits, NaN where masked). noise="varying" in fit_lorentzian , fit_two_modes and fit_map : error bars from the heteroskedasticity-consistent ("sandwich") covariance of H. White, Econometrica 48, 817 (1980), for spectra whose noise level changes along the axis, as shot noise does. Fitted values are unchanged. On 600 seeded Poisson spectra the center scatter is 1.7 times the default error bar and within 10 % of the new one; checked also against an independent finite-difference sandwich (relative 1e-5). The default, noise="constant" , is unchanged. README example 18 (shot noise) and a "Tutorials" section. Fixed calibrate_lever_arms , plan_calibration and design_references judged identifiability from the raw singular values of the design, which depends on the units. Before: the six-state design of the tests with the density in cm^-2 raised ValueError: reference states are collinear ... ( plan_calibration returned identifiable=False ). After: it gives the arms of the fit in 1e13 cm^-2, rescaled (A'1 density arm -2.2798e-13 per cm^-2 against -2.2798 per 1e13 cm^-2; relative 1e-10). The test is now made on the design with unit-length columns (also with fit_offset=True ). Test: test_calibration_does_not_depend_on_the_density_unit , test_planning_does_not_depend_on_the_density_unit . bayesian_map_inversion(..., fill_masked=True) : the same unit dependence in its pooled-information check. Before: a lever-arm matrix with the density column in cm^-2 raised ValueError: ... their pooled information matrix is singular . After: the filled pixel's density is 0.50185398920 (x 1e13 cm^-2), against 0.50185398920 with the density in 1e13 cm^-2 (largest relative difference over the map 2.5e-7). Test: test_bayesian_fill_masked_does_not_depend_on_the_density_unit . compare_mode_sets with subset_size 0, 1 or larger than the number of modes returned [] ; it now raises ValueError (also for a non-integer size, which raised TypeError ). Test: test_compare_mode_sets_refuses_a_subset_size_it_cannot_rank . Documentation: the fitting module, the README "What is in the package" and "Limits" said the peak-fit error ba
title: ramansep: two-mode separation of strain and carrier density in 2D-material Raman maps

summary: Added inverse_predict(model, result, reading, bracket, reading_sigma=0.0, theta=None, cov=None, n_scan=1001, max_slope_change=0.1) : reads a calibration curve backwards. It finds the setting x0 at which the model predicts a new reading inside the given bracket (a scan of n_scan points for sign changes, then bisection) and its error bar by first-order propagation through the implicit function, u(x0)^2 = (u(y0)^2 + a^T C a) / s^2 (JCGM 100:2008, section 5.2), split into the part from the reading and the part from the calibration. Several readings give the full covariance (they share the calibration). For a straight line it is the propagation-of-error formula of the NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook of Statistical Methods, section 2.3.6.7.3 (https://itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/mpc/section3/mpc3673.htm). Refuses a reading the model does not reach in the bracket or reaches more than once, a model that is flat at the solution, and a solution where the slope changes by more than max_slope_change (10 %) within one error bar, where a first-order error bar is not reliable. runs_test(residuals, order=None) : the runs test of A. Wald and J. Wolfowitz, Ann. Math. Statist. 11, 147-162 (1940), doi:10.1214/aoms/1177731909, on the signs of the residuals ordered by the setting. Finds a systematic misfit (a bend, a drift) that chi-squared misses when the reading errors are overstated. Exact tail probabilities of the number of runs, p_value (too few runs) and p_value_high (too many), with the mean and standard deviation of the number of runs. Tutorials examples/tutorial_calibration_curve.py and examples/tutorial_decay_on_background.py (see Tutorials below). README examples 13 ( inverse_predict ) and 14 ( runs_test ), and a Tutorials section, each with output obtained by running it. Fixed Model.numeric_jacobian (and so information , design , fit and propagate ) refused a valid model at a valid parameter as "non-finite". A parameter whose relative step does not change the predictions by 1e-8 of their largest value falls back to the 0.1.0 step 1e-6 * max(|theta|, 1e-3) , which is 1e-9 for a parameter below 1e-3: for a time constant of 1e-9 s it is the parameter itself. A decay of amplitude 10 on a background of 1000 (any amplitude below about 1/73 of the background), tau = 1e-9 s, samples from t = 0: tau - h = 0 , the model divided 0 by 0, and before the fix information , design and fit from that guess raised "the forward function returned non-finite predictions". After: the step is divided by 10 until the model is finite (at most 8 times) and then checked as before; the planned error bar on tau (reading error 1) is 1.4189183e-10 s, the exact value from the analytic slopes to 6e-9 relative, and the fit equals the fit with exact slopes to 1e-4 of an error bar. Steps that already gave finite predictions are used as before, so every result 0.3.0 could compute is unchanged (test test_fallback_step_that_reaches_zero_is_cut , which fails on 0.3.0, and test_fallback_cut_does_not_touch_working_steps ). Changed Clearer refusals: Model.numeric_jacobian (which Model.jacobian uses when the model has no jac ) refuses a rel_step that is not a finite positive number (0.3.0 raised UnboundLocalError for 0 or a negative step); coverage_exact refuses an n that is not a whole number (0.3.0 returned 0.9 for coverage_exact(29.9, 0.1) , the answer for n = 29). Packaging (from the unreleased notes after 0.3.0): the license is given as the SPDX expression license = "Apache-2.0" with license-files = ["LICENSE"] ; the old license table and license classifier are gone. Building no longer prints setuptools' deprecation warnings (their support ends on 2027-02-18). Building from source needs setuptools 77 or newer; installing the package is unchanged. README: the new functions, refusals, tests, the 0.4.0 correction, limits and sources; a word guide entry for residuals and runs and one for inverse prediction. The printed output of README examples 1

summary: Analysis of Ly-Algebraic 5-Fold Symmetry Coherence and Sequestration Efficiency in Autonomous Multi-Agent Swarm Systems   C. J Tully Independent Researcher Engineer Tamworth, NSW, Australia ORCID: 0009-0007-5661-7332 chloetully5@gmail.com     ---   Abstract   This paper presents a comprehensive empirical analysis of dual-swarm autonomous systems operating under the Ly-Algebraic 5-Fold Symmetry framework, examining the relationship between S₅ coherence metrics, optimal connectivity parameters (K), and sequestration efficiency over 500 simulation timesteps. The study investigates two distinct swarm architectures—Swarm A, demonstrating convergent evolutionary behavior, and Swarm B, exhibiting persistent oscillatory dynamics. Statistical analysis reveals Swarm A achieves mean S₅ coherence of 0.734 (SD = 0.171) with sequestration efficiency reaching 79.8% (SD = 14.2%), while Swarm B maintains significantly lower coherence (M = 0.180, SD = 0.052) and sequestration efficiency (M = 7.7%, SD = 4.1%). Correlation analysis demonstrates strong positive relationships between coherence and sequestration efficiency in both swarms (Swarm A: r = 0.972, p < 0.001; Swarm B: r = 0.621, p < 0.001). Temporal analysis reveals phase-transition dynamics in Swarm A characterized by three distinct epochs of stabilization. The optimal K parameter exhibits inverse correlation with coherence maturation in Swarm A, decreasing from modal values of 7-8 during early phases to 1-2 during stabilization epochs. These findings validate the theoretical predictions of pentagonal symmetry coherence convergence and provide empirical foundations for quantum-resilient autonomous intelligence architectures.   Keywords: Ly-Algebraic 5-Fold Symmetry, swarm coherence, sequestration efficiency, autonomous systems, Z₅-grading, post-quantum cryptography   ---   1. The NOUS_ONE framework establishes critical requirements for maintaining tamper-evident context preservation while simultaneously achieving high sequestration efficiency—a measure of a system's capacity to capture and retain essential state information during autonomous operation.   This study presents empirical analysis of 500 simulation timesteps examining two distinct swarm architectures operating under the Ly-Algebraic framework. Swarm A represents a convergent configuration demonstrating progressive coherence stabilization, while Swarm B exhibits persistent oscillatory behavior characteristic of unstable attractor dynamics. summary: Hashing, signing, and timestamping establish that a document has not changed. When a legal document is produced by composition, from templates, clause libraries, shared definitions, and parameters that evolve independently, the governing text is a resolved state, and the integrity of the root document does not ensure that this state can be reconstructed. We treat this as a problem of ex post auditability. We define the resolved state as S_t = ρ(A_0, R_t, C_t), derive five properties of its auditability from requirements established in archival science, legal document standards, and norm-change formalisms, and introduce a capture model K_t with a diagnostic procedure that reports which properties a capture fails. We implement the framework in cmacc-attest and apply it to the 175 instantiated contracts of the CommonAccord library. References resolve in 96.6% of contracts, yet none is auditable: no reference is version-locked, and 98.3% contain conflicts settled by an unattested precedence order. Replaying 194 commits of the library history shows that 88.5% of the changes in resolved contracts left the root file unchanged. Repository history narrows reconstruction when the time of resolution is known, but does not replace a capture.
title: Beyond Document Integrity: Auditing Resolved States of Formalized Legal Documents

summary: MULTI-AGENT ROUTING OF NEUROVASCULAR MICROROBOT SWARMS AT THE LIMIT This research monograph develops a falsifiable, non-clinical framework for routing heterogeneous microrobotic teams through branching neurovascular vessel phantoms. It asks whether decentralized task assignment, flow-aware navigation, independently tracked agent identity, and verifiable recovery can improve qualified sensing or inert-sample collection without increasing collision, occlusion, flow disturbance, thermal burden, sample confusion, or residual material risk. Organized around low-Reynolds-number hydrodynamics, multi-agent coordination, and independently enforced physical safety boundaries, the volume contains 30 mathematical derivation plates, 82 full research chapters with five separately paginated sections each, 200 detailed Research Gates, and 33 provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos. A DOI evidence ledger distinguishes established component physics and published demonstrations from the original system-level hypotheses proposed here. Strong passive-transport, single-agent, and information-matched centralized alternatives remain valid competitors throughout. Research failures, abandoned models, experimental uncertainty, and successor reconstruction are treated as scientific outputs, not editorial defects. The monograph provides a research architecture and prospective tests, not results from experiments performed for this publication. It does not assert demonstrated autonomous navigation in human cerebral vessels, clinical safety, therapeutic efficacy, or authorization for human intervention.

summary: Absorption and scattering coefficients for the Jerlov optical water types, taken from the primary literature with the provenance of every value recorded. Values that a published table got wrong are flagged rather than silently repaired, and quantities the data do not determine are refused rather than guessed. Twenty-three entries are documented, nine of them confirmed defects in the source literature: duplicated rows in Solonenko & Mobley (2015) Table 7, a transcription error in the small-particle scattering coefficient that propagated into their published coefficients, a Data Availability Statement that gives the DOI of an unrelated dataset, and a reprint whose stated unit is out by a factor of ten. Three further entries were open questions that obtaining the 1968 first edition settled. The same Jerlov water type is in circulation with beam attenuations differing by a factor of five, which is why every coefficient here carries the source it came from. Every shipped table can be regenerated from its primary source by the scripts in tools/ , and each generation step checks the result against the equations of the paper it came from. The package computes the direct and veiling components along a horizontal underwater path, converts spectra to CIE XYZ, sRGB, or the response of an arbitrary camera or set of photoreceptors, gives the Jerlov type that typically applies in each 10 m layer down to 200 m and carries the downwelling irradiance down through those layers, integrates photosynthetically available radiation (PAR), or the photon flux over any other band or weighted by any spectral sensitivity, with depth, gives the spectrum at any depth and the effective Kd between two, and finds the depth at which PAR falls to 1 percent, ranks the Jerlov types by their distance from a measured Kd spectrum, carries Jerlov's measured profiles of quanta irradiance (350-700 nm) by water type and checks the depth profile against them, carries Tyler's (1958) measured radiance distribution in Lake Pend Oreille, carries the Paulson & Simpson (1977) shortwave penetration parameters used by ocean circulation models, converts a backscattering sensor's single-angle reading into the backscattering coefficient, and carries Petzold's (1972) volume scattering functions for eight measured ocean waters.

summary: Coding agents can now interpret a specification, implement it, write and execute tests, repair failures, and declare the result ready for release. When the same agentic system produces both the software and the evidence of its correctness, a passing test suite no longer constitutes independent evidence. Visible tests become an optimization target, and code, tests, and oracles may share a single misinterpretation of the specification. This paper argues that agent-produced software requires an assurance plane that is structurally independent of the build plane. We first characterize four gaps along the chain from stakeholder intent to production, namely the requirement, conformance, evaluation, and model gaps, and identify which of them verification can close. We then propose a framework that separates building from verifying, introduces a Verification Contract stating what must be demonstrated before release, and organizes verification in two phases: a specification-first phase designed without access to the implementation, and an implementation-aware phase that strengthens the evidence through mutation analysis, property-based testing, and fuzzing. The resulting evidence is consolidated into an assurance report that makes residual uncertainty explicit and leaves the release decision to a human. We evaluate the framework in a pre-registered study on three stateful services, two of them written by third-party models, and an EvalPlus pilot, comparing self-validation with independent verification under context-level and model-level independence. The builder's programs were correct, but its own tests missed subtle interactions: a verifier in a fresh context detected more of the 46 seeded faults than the builder's tests (Holm-corrected p = 0.006), and surfaced the ambiguities of the specification, at the price of rare false oracles. A verifier from another provider did not add detection. The framework and the study provide a basis for governing the release of software produced by agents.
title: Who Verifies the Builder? Toward Independent Assurance for Agent-Produced Software

summary: Code, archived production results and figure scripts that reproduce the numbers and figures of two companion papers on a small flat universe, a cubic three-torus that begins at a Casimir turning point: A. Zhang, Gauge Field Fluctuations Protect the Higgs Vacuum When a Small Universe Begins (2026), a Letter; A. Zhang, A Casimir turning point as the beginning of a small flat universe (2026). The companion technical report, A. Zhang, Casimir Cosmology: Derivations and Numerical Validation, version 1.0 (2026), is deposited as a separate record, https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23434140; a copy is included in docs/technical_report/. Contents. Four chains of result directories: casimir/ (Standard Model Casimir weight, gauge and Higgs zero-mode energy, shape Hessian), higgs/ (finite-volume criterion for the Higgs zero mode: Standard Model couplings at the turning-point scale, one-loop finite-volume matching, two-dimensional zero-mode model with cross terms, hazard integral, critical top-quark masses and error budget, real-time ξ_H condition, robustness, universality, two-branch analysis), shape/ (emptiness gate, real-moment theorem, shape fossil, nonlinear survival, Moyal and Wheeler–DeWitt checks, primordial spectra) and cmb/ (temperature and polarization covariance of a three-torus, Fisher information and exact Kullback–Leibler divergences, fossil ensemble, joint inflaton–shape state). Every result directory has a quick and a full mode and compares fresh output with the archived production values under stated tolerances; python run_all.py --quick reproduces the quick checks and all figures. validation/ archives the independent reimplementations of the main results, with their specifications, code and outputs, and compares them with the main calculation. numbers/ is the single source of the numbers quoted in the papers and in the report. cmb/02_ensemble/data/ contains the ℓ ≤ 80 CAMB transfer table. Verification. On a fresh copy of this release (Python 3.12, Windows 11), python run_all.py --quick passes in all 25 verification runs (241 of 242 checks passed, 1 optional check skipped: the compiled SMDR refit), and the 51 shared numbers of the papers and the report (numbers/) agree with the archived outputs. Details and known limitations are given in RELEASE_NOTES.md. Integrity. MANIFEST.json and SHA256SUMS.txt list the size and SHA-256 of every file; python tools/sha256sums.py check verifies a copy. This record archives release v1.0.0 of https://github.com/Ailun-Zhang/casimir-cosmology. Licenses. Code: MIT. Data and text: CC BY 4.0. The SMDR 1.3 tarball (shipped unmodified) and the four files derived from or linked against it: GPL-2.0-or-later (see README.md, section License).

summary: This is the replication package of the paper Required to Test or Inspired to Test? A Survey of the Socio-Technical Conditions of Software Testing . The paper reports a survey of 52 software developers on how organizational, technical and social conditions relate to their motivation to test and to how extensively they test. It validates the survey instrument and tests eight hypotheses that we published before data collection. Contents File Contents Registered Instrument.pdf Anonymized copy of the report in which we published the survey instrument and the hypotheses before we began data collection data.csv Anonymized survey responses, exported from Qualtrics with answer labels export.zip Figures and tables the paper refers to, exported from the web application web-application-source.tar.gz Source code of the interactive web application that we used for the validation and the analysis, with unit tests and installation instructions Registered report To keep the review double-blind, the copy differs from the published report in the following points: We removed the names and affiliation of the authors. We changed the title and reworded the abstract. The research questions, hypotheses and survey questions are unchanged. The paper discusses where the study deviates from this report. Survey data The first three rows of data.csv hold the column names, the question texts and Qualtrics import identifiers. The file contains all recorded responses. The web application selects the responses the paper analyzes in the following steps: Step Responses All recorded responses, including unfinished responses, survey previews, responses without consent and the pilot study 126 Finished responses of participants who gave their consent, without previews and pilot responses (before 10 September 2025) 57 Without the participants who work on solo projects, analyzed in the paper 52 Figures and tables export.zip contains all figures in one PDF ( figures.pdf ) and as separate files, and the tables as CSV files. Its README.md lists the same overview. Content Section of the paper File in export.zip Decisions on all survey items that were removed, reassigned, or kept despite a low value III tables/item_decisions.csv Eigenvalue and loading range of the first component of each scale III tables/eigenvalues_and_loadings.csv Scree plot of each scale III figures.pdf , figures/scree-plot-of-*.pdf Demographics of the participants IV figures.pdf , figures/demographics.pdf Boxplots of all variables IV figures.pdf , figures/boxplots-of-all-variables.pdf All hypothesis tests with statistics, effect sizes, uncorrected and corrected p-values, and verdicts IV tables/all_tests.csv Running the web application The web application requires Python 3.10 or later and Poetry . tar -xzf web-application-source.tar.gz cd <extracted folder> poetry install cp <path to>/data.csv data/data.csv poetry run invoke run The application then runs at http://localhost:8501 . README.md in the source code describes further tasks, such as invoke export , which recreates the contents of export.zip .

summary: Every element of the causal chain that produced the five largest mass extinctions of the last half-billion years is presently accelerating in the Earth system. The rate of the modern perturbation exceeds every peer-reviewed paleoclimate reference case. A six-intervention portfolio, deployed together at wartime industrial scale beginning now, is the physically necessary and sufficient response. The window in which that portfolio remains fully effective closes between 2028 and 2040. The anthropogenic-versus-feedback tipping point is expected between 2035 and 2040; corrected for the at-least-order-of-magnitude higher rate of contemporary carbon release, loss of agency — the point at which coordinated intervention can no longer arrest the cascade — arrives 200 to 400 years after feedback engagement under sustained portfolio deployment, and collapses onto the tipping point itself under any scenario in which the portfolio is not deployed within the 2028–2040 window. Background. The five largest mass-extinction events of the Phanerozoic share a consistent causal chain: rapid carbon injection to the ocean-atmosphere system, followed by warming, ocean deoxygenation, acidification, and preferential loss of marine calcifiers, with multi-million-year recovery for reef ecosystems. Every element of that chain is presently active and gaining speed. The current anthropogenic perturbation is capable of driving a combination and magnitude of ocean geochemical changes unparalleled in the geological record reviewed by Hönisch et al. (2012), which covers approximately the past 300 million years. The reef–ocean-oxygen–land coupling documented in the End-Permian record demonstrates that marine biosphere collapse propagates to terrestrial extinction through the shared oxygen and biogeochemical infrastructure of the coupled Earth system; contemporary marine indicators are therefore leading indicators of terrestrial as well as marine risk. Approach. This three-part synthesis compiles peer-reviewed reconstructions of the Big Five causal chain, measures each element against the contemporary Earth system using the most recent authoritative data (Friedlingstein et al. 2026; Wu et al. 2021; Zeebe et al. 2016; Hönisch et al. 2012; Schmidtko et al. 2017; Eddy et al. 2021; Spady et al. 2026), specifies the physically necessary intervention portfolio, and characterizes the near-term feedback, resource, and civilizational risk environment those interventions must succeed in. Part I establishes the paleoclimate analog. Part II specifies the intervention portfolio. Part III maps the contemporary Earth system the Part II portfolio must succeed in — which climate feedbacks are already engaged and how they cascade, which physical resources are hitting hard limits inside the same two-to-three-decade window, and how those pressures translate into food, water, migration, health, economic, and governance strain — and closes with the North American Climate Pain Scale (NAPS), a 1–10 diagnostic instrument that anchors climate severity to concrete events so policymakers and the public can locate today's conditions and the trajectory ahead. Findings. Every element of the paleoclimate extinction causal chain is presently active. Atmospheric CO₂ (422.8 ppm, 2024 global annual mean; Friedlingstein et al. 2026) has exceeded the reconstructed latest-Permian baseline of 426 (+133 / −96) ppm (Wu et al. 2021, Nature Communications). The rate of contemporary carbon release is at least an order of magnitude above the sustained maximum Paleocene-Eocene Thermal Maximum rate (Zeebe, Ridgwell and Zachos 2016, Nature Geoscience). Ocean acidification is proceeding at roughly ten times the PETM rate (Hönisch et al. 2012, Science). The global ocean has lost 4.8 ± 2.1 petamoles of dissolved oxygen since 1960 (Schmidtko, Stramma and Visbeck 2017, Nature). summary: Climate change affects human well-being through interacting physical, ecological, infrastructural, and socioeconomic processes rather than through a single exposure or disease pathway. Major assessments identify observed harms to health, food and water security, livelihoods, settlements, and ecosystems, alongside increasing risks with additional warming (IPCC, 2022a). This narrative review develops a cross-sector framework from a source inventory of 154 human-impact pathways in 14 domains, supported by major assessments, selected peer-reviewed studies, and institutional datasets. Literature selection used targeted web-index searches and source verification through 2 October 2026; the review does not estimate pooled effects or claim exhaustive systematic coverage. The synthesis distinguishes direct injury and illness, ecosystem-mediated harms, failures of essential services, financial transmission, and losses of social and cultural continuity. Representative quantitative findings illustrate substantial existing burdens, but attribution studies, ecological associations, exposure models, displacement records, and conditional forecasts measure different quantities and cannot be combined into a universal five-year trajectory (Vicedo-Cabrera et al., 2021; Wang et al., 2026; Clement et al., 2021). Compound hazards and service interdependencies can increase losses beyond the directly affected sector, while repeated shocks can reduce the capacity to recover or adapt (Zscheischler et al., 2018; IPCC, 2023). A reporting framework is proposed that records the outcome, population, baseline, geography, time horizon, emissions and development assumptions, adaptation, and uncertainty for each indicator. The central contribution is an integrated interpretation and measurement architecture, not a new forecast of global mortality, migration, or societal collapse. Effective assessment should preserve evidence of serious and interacting harms without converting uncertain thresholds or heterogeneous studies into unsupported calendar-specific predictions.

summary: Reconstructing Earth's deep-time paleoclimate record provides a critical framework for evaluating modern anthropogenic climate forcing. Here, we synthesize proxy records from the "Big Five" mass extinction events—Late Ordovician (LOME), Late Devonian, Permian-Triassic (PTME), Triassic-Jurassic (TJME), and Cretaceous-Paleogene (K-Pg)—and evaluate their proxy signals against modern biogeochemical trends. While cumulative carbon emissions during deep-time hyperthermals were larger in absolute magnitude, current annual carbon injection rates ( ∼ 10 G t C / y e a r ) and global warming velocities ( ∼ 0.2° C / d e c a d e ) exceed reconstructed pre-extinction baselines by factors of 10x to 100x. We catalog 17 positive climate feedback loops, 16 of which are currently active, and apply an Earth System Feedback Framework to demonstrate that integrating biogeochemical and cryospheric tipping dynamics elevates standard Equilibrium Climate Sensitivity ( E C S ≈ 3.0° C ) to an Earth System Sensitivity gain factor of G E S S ≈ 4.76 ( E S S ≈ 4.0–5.0° C for doubled C O 2 ). Synthesizing this feedback framework with Earth system tipping point literature (e.g., Armstrong McKay et al., 2022; Steffen et al., 2018; Kemp et al., 2022), we use this feedback gain function to model the boundary and evaluate the risk horizon for reaching a "Point of Human Agency Loss"—defined as the biogeochemical threshold where autonomous natural feedback emissions ( ≥ 10.0 G t C O 2 e / y e a r ) match or exceed maximum technological human mitigation and carbon removal capacity. We establish that crossing the 1.5° C to 2.0° C global warming horizon (projected mid-century) shifts the Earth system into a self-sustaining feedback regime. Driven by coupled biophysical stress vectors (niche thermal limits, crop yield collapses, and hydrological contraction; Xu et al., 2020) and the non-linear carrying-capacity decay function K ( T ) , human support capacity is projected to contract non-linearly from baseline Holocene levels ( ∼ 8.5–9.0 b i l l i o n ) to an equilibrium ceiling of ∼ 1.3–1.5 b i l l i o n at a stabilized state ( +3.3–3.5° C ). Finally, we perform a Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) across 16 proposed climate interventions, evaluating scale, cost, geopolitical friction, termination shock, and moral hazard risk. We conclude that while physical variables (temperature, ocean pH) may be geochemically reversible over centuries via solar radiation management and permanent carbon removal, biospheric destruction, species extinction, and sea-level commitment exhibit severe hysteresis (path-dependence where a system fails to return to its initial state even if forcing is removed), making damage containment rather than ecosystem restoration the primary operational objective.

summary: Shincheonji Church of Jesus (commonly Shincheonji) is a new Christian millenarian church established in 1984 by Lee Man-hee (b. 1931) in South Korea. Shincheonji is an abbreviation of the phrase sincheongukjigu (신천국지구) which translates to 'New Heaven New Earth,' a reference to Revelation 21:1. Shincheonji can also be classified as a grassroots Korean religious movement or form of Christianity due to its development in South Korea, its close connections to earlier Korean millenarian Christian movements, and the they understand the South Korean nation as the location in which the prophecies contained Revelation have been fulfilled. Although South Korea is home to more members of Shincheonji than any other country, it is an international church with members and locations across Asia, Africa, Europe, the Americas, and Oceania. This entry, however, is focused on the Korean context. While the church has always been the subject of mass media attention and public scrutiny in South Korea, it gained the attention of international news media in February 2020 when a Covid-19 cluster infection in the city of Daegu was traced to one of its members. Shincheonji is often labelled as 'idan' (or 'heresy') or saibi jonggyo (which can be translated to 'pseudo-religion') by critical and 'anti-cult' Protestant theologians and pastors we well as in mainstream news and entertainment media. Shincheonji teachings that the prophecies of Revelations have already been fulfilled in South Korea in the 20th century, with the founder, Lee Man-hee (or Chairman Lee to members) as the witness these events. Although Christ's second coming is yet to occur, Shincheonji teaches that the old heaven and earth will give way to the new heaven and the new earth (which is Shincheonji). The 144,000 elect will dwell in the millennial kingdom: the holy city of the new Jerusalem. To bring about the Second Coming, it is understood that humans must work with God to create a peaceful world that mirrors heaven. While this entry attempts to outline key features, beliefs, and practices within Shincheonji as well as their social, cultural, and political engagements, this is complicated by Shincheonji's strategies of knowledge protection and information management. As a marginalised and minority religious community within South Korea, members can face harsh social, economic, and physical consequences should their faith commitments be revealed. As a result, Shincheonji is very careful about sharing information due to fears of negative public perceptions. Shincheonji also believes that knowledge of biblical truth offers salvation and eternal life, and thus access to this knowledge must be carefully managed.

summary: This reproducibility archive accompanies Marco Mantovanelli's A Multi-Arch Perturbed Hofstadter Q-Recursion: Gaussian Profiles and Exact Frequency Laws. It contains the manuscript PDF, complete LaTeX source, six vector figures, independent verification programs, figure-generation code, numerical reports, and sampled figure data. The paper studies Q(n) = Q(n - Q(n-1)) + Q(n - Q(n-2)) - (-1)^n for n >= 8, with the seven prescribed initial values (1, 1, 3, 3, 3, 3, 5). A causal binary-word construction proves global existence and an exact factorization into three signed excursions. Their uniformly convergent Gaussian profiles explain three limiting sign transitions per standard dyadic block and a sharp normalized error envelope of approximately 0.067088003576. The paper also proves exact finite transition locations, an ordered frequency factorization, a shifted 2-adic valuation law on pure dyadic value blocks, and a summatory asymptotic with an explicit continuous periodic term. The archived verification compares all 33,554,432 directly computed terms with an independent word reconstruction, checks complete frequency blocks through level 21, and verifies the exact summatory identity at every even cutoff from 8 through 33,554,432. Separate programs audit the word maps, finite transitions, and exact two-head identities. These computations supplement the general proofs in the manuscript. The original perturbation, OEIS A394051, is discussed for comparison.
title: A Multi-Arch Perturbed Hofstadter Q-Recursion: Gaussian Profiles and Exact Frequency Laws (Reproducibility Archive)

summary: Modern automatic speaker verification (ASV) systems are vulnerable to adversarial perturbations. Diffusion-based purification has recently shown strong effectiveness against such perturbations, but its reverse denoising process requires iterative sampling and leads to high inference latency. We find that the forward noising process provides most of the robustness gain. Motivated by this observation, we reformulate adversarial purification as a learnable noising problem, and propose the Positive-Incentive Noise Predictor (PnP), the first framework that explicitly introduces positive-incentive noise (π-noise) into the purification task. PnP learns input-adaptive π-noise and mixes it with the input to improve the robustness of downstream ASV systems. Experiments on four advanced ASV backbones show that PnP effectively defends against adversarial attacks while preserving performance on natural speech. Compared with representative purification baselines, the proposed framework provides a competitive balance among defense effectiveness, impact on genuine utterances, and inference efficiency under white-box, black-box, and defender-aware adaptive attacks, with a real-time factor as low as 0.014. Moreover, PnP can be cascaded with a diffusion denoiser to further improve the perceptual quality of purified utterances. Code and purified audio examples are available at https://eurecom-asp.github.io/pnp/
title: Positive-Incentive Noise Predictor for Adversarial Purification in Speaker Verification

summary: The Empty Occupant: Answerability, Testimony, and the Limits of Machine-Mediated Authority examines a problem of institutional AI: automated decisions can scale faster than institutions' capacity to justify, reconsider, correct, or repair them. Identifying a responsible institution does not establish that its decisions were warrantedly adopted or that resulting obligations can be discharged. Across philosophy of language, social epistemology, social ontology, normative theory, AI governance, and administrative law , the monograph develops a substrate-neutral Discursive Ontology connecting three questions: who bears an institutional commitment, what warrants its adoption, and whether answerability can be sustained at scale. It distinguishes commitment ownership, warranted adoption, adequate discharge, causal contribution, and legal liability. Five contributions follow: Discursive Ontology and Answerability. Defines commitment-bearing through four jointly necessary relations within reciprocal normative standing: attribution continuity, challenge-responsive reconsideration, repair competence, and standing-consequence . It distinguishes Actual, Residual, Prospective, and Empty Occupancy . Empty Occupancy requires presentation as an independent bearer and affirmative evidence that the relevant standing is absent , not a mere machine interface. The axiom is that missing bearership is not defective ownership : a principal may remain responsible for commitments its interface cannot independently bear. Testimony Without a Testifier. Separates hearer-side epistemic uptake from speaker-side commitment ownership . Machine outputs can inform without establishing an answerable speaker. On assurance-based accounts, they can exercise testimonial force without constituting testimony . Reliability, fluency, and conversational memory alone confer no authority to retract a commitment. Normative Sponsorship. Specifies five conditions for warranted institutional adoption: epistemic access, authority, review bandwidth, independent rejection, and repair power . Its contestation-grain opacity threshold requires reconstructing relevant grounds where a challenge must take effect—at input, case, rule, shared-premise, or architecture—without complete transparency. It distinguishes technical opacity from organizational capture , where reasons are knowable but cannot bind, and considers model succession and agentic chains. Deontic Debt and Institutional Insolvency. Derives consequence-sensitive reconsideration from the defeasibility of presumptive authority. Deontic Debt comprises matured obligations deficiently serviced, not simply pending work. Institutional Insolvency arises when no credible service plan meets relevant obligations and protections for a specified claim mix, issuance scale, lawful architecture, and horizon. Its consequence is targeted loss of presumptive authority , not automatic legal invalidity or release from ownership and repair duties. Institutional Stewardship. Connects permissible automated use to warranted sponsorship, protective review, binding reconsideration, and effective repair. Restoration requires legacy discharge, demonstrable future capacity, and scaled resumption. Public-record analyses examine Australia's Robodebt scheme, Moffatt v. Air Canada , A.M.C. v. Smith (TennCare), the Post Office Horizon scandal, the Dutch childcare-benefits affair, and a press-based DPD generative-interface episode. Neither Air Canada nor DPD establishes determinate Empty Occupancy. summary: We develop a rigorous reduction inside the Connes–Consani–Moscovici programme for the Riemann hypothesis. The main unconditional result is the following symmetry principle: for the truncated Weil quadratic form QW_λ^N, simplicity of the lowest eigenvalue ε_N implies evenness of the corresponding ground state ξ, provided the natural reflection symmetry γV_n = V_{-n} and the normalization ℓ_N(ξ) = 1 are imposed. This converts two structural requirements of the programme into one spectral requirement. We then prove a precise spectral approximation criterion. If the finite-dimensional form QW_λ^N approximates the prolate wave operator PW_λ in a form-strong sense sufficient to preserve the first isolated simple eigenvalue, then ε_N is simple for all large N. Combining this criterion with the symmetry principle gives evenness of the ground state. Finally, we prove a windowed determinant criterion for the Riemann hypothesis. If the regularized determinants attached to the Connes–Consani–Moscovici finite-rank perturbations have only real zeros and converge locally uniformly, on an exhausting family of windows, to nonzero multiples of the Riemann Ξ-function, then every zero of Ξ is real, and therefore the Riemann hypothesis follows. The paper separates cleanly the proved logical reductions from the analytic objectives required for their unconditional verification. Those objectives are collected in a final section of open problems, giving a foundational reference for the remaining work in the programme. We emphasize that this paper does not claim an unconditional proof of the Riemann hypothesis; rather, it provides a precise structural reduction and isolates the remaining analytic challenges.
title: Evenness from Simplicity in the Truncated Weil Quadratic Form and Conditional Spectral Criteria for the Riemann Hypothesis

summary: International business (IB) theory explains how firms enter foreign markets, allocate ownership, govern cross-border activities, build networks, and accumulate market knowledge. Less explicit attention has been given to the internationalization of the firm’s continuing operating system itself. This article develops the concept of operational internationalization: the cross-border extension of recurring fulfilment, inventory, logistics, service, compliance, and information processes, regardless of whether the underlying capabilities are fully owned by the focal firm. It further introduces operational embeddedness and boundary asymmetry to explain why ownership, governance, operational, and jurisdictional boundaries may overlap without expanding synchronously. Sovereign jurisdiction is treated as a constitutive boundary because tax, customs, data, product, environmental, and related rules shape which cross-border configurations are institutionally admissible. The framework becomes dynamic through reverse value-information flow, whereby economically consequential market and jurisdictional information generated abroad enters subsequent production, allocation, service, and organizational decisions. Just-in-Place (JIP) is positioned within this architecture as the enactment logic through which geographically and institutionally dispersed capabilities are selectively activated and recombined. A comparative public-disclosure analysis of Linamar and JD Logistics provides complementary evidence of inward informational feedback and outward operational extension. The article reconceptualizes internationalization as a reflexive, multi-boundary process in which the operating system itself becomes an analytically distinct object of cross-border expansion.
title: Internationalizing the Operating System: Operational Embeddedness, Jurisdictional Boundaries, and Just-in-Place

summary: No contexto atual de valorização das práticas sustentáveis e da eficiência operacional, a logística reversa apresenta-se como uma ferramenta estratégica na gestão de resíduos sólidos em ambientes aeroportuários. O presente estudo tem como objetivo analisar os principais desafios relacionados à logística reversa no Aeroporto Internacional de São Paulo/Guarulhos, bem como avaliar o uso de tecnologias aplicadas à logística como forma de otimização dos processos. A metodologia adotada baseia-se em revisão bibliográfica e análise de estudos de caso. Os resultados demonstram que a ausência de um sistema integrado de gestão de resíduos, aliada à baixa utilização de tecnologias, compromete a eficiência operacional e gera perdas financeiras. Como proposta, sugere-se a implantação de um sistema inteligente de monitoramento de resíduos com uso de Internet das Coisas (IoT), visando aumentar a eficiência da coleta seletiva e o reaproveitamento de materiais.
title: Logística Reversa e Tecnologia Aplicada no Aeroporto Internacional de Guarulhos: Desafios e Soluções Operacionais

summary: Code, trained weights and campaign results for the paper "Morphological diffusion by ball births: generative models of binary images with exact Betti increments" by M. Zéraï, submitted to the Journal of Mathematical Imaging and Vision. The model generates binary images by births of maximal balls. Its forward process is a random granulometry, and its reverse process learns a birth map. morpho_repro.tar.gz contains the implementation (model, sampler, exact Euler increments, measurement protocol), the averaged (EMA) weights of all trained models on the three datasets (GRF, BBBC039 nuclei masks, MNIST), the campaign reports and logs, and the GRF data. README.md gives the hyperparameters, the source of each table and the reproduction commands. figs_print.tar.gz contains the figure boards of the paper with their statistics. The BBBC039 masks and MNIST are public and are downloaded by prepare_data.sh. Note: the two archives are gzip-compressed tar files, deposited as morpho_repro.tar and figs_print.tar (README.md names them morpho_repro.tar.gz and figs_print.tar.gz). Extract them with: tar xzf morpho_repro.tar
title: Morphological diffusion by ball births: code, trained weights and campaign results
