Temperatures are given both as raw values (suffix "_raw") and as values corrected through a cross-calibration of the three stations. The file also gives air and ground temperature differences between stations: B−A (uncoated minus coated pav
title: Influence of land cover and shade on the thermal environments of schoolyards in Los Angeles

summary: Fisher information metric tensors for the 41 held-out SONICOM test subjects, as used in “Evaluating Spatial Discriminability Preservation in HRTF Upsampling Using Fisher Information” (D. Bassett). Code and reproduction instructions: https://github.com/domfrbassett/fisher-rao-hrtf-upsampling What the tensors are At each of the 793 directions of the SONICOM grid, the 2×2 tensor g = JᵀΣ⁻¹J describes how well the auditory cues separate that direction from its neighbours. J is the spatial Jacobian of the cues: Barumerli monaural PGE features, ILD and MaxIACCe-transformed ITD, each fitted with real spherical harmonics. Σ holds the cue noise (σ_mon = 1.25 dB, σ_ILD = 1 dB, σ_ITD = 0.569). All fields are low-pass filtered at 16 kHz before the cues are extracted. The tensor is expressed in a local tangent basis u₁ = a × r, u₂ = r × u₁, where a = z, or y when |r_z| > 0.9, and its units are d′² per rad². Contents metric_tensors.zip has one folder per subject, metric_tensors/subject_####/ , containing 25 files per subject (1,025 in total): reference_metric_tensor.mat : the dense measured HRTF. <METHOD>_N###_metric_tensor.mat : one file per reconstruction. There are six methods: SUpDEq_SH , SUpDEq_MCA , SUpDEq_NN_MCA_6dB (SUpDEq-Natural-MCA in the paper), SUpDEq_Bary_MCA_6dB , RANF and FSP_AE . Each is reconstructed from N = 100, 19, 5 and 3 retained directions. The 164 natural-neighbour and barycentric files at N = 5 and 3 have status “ not_applicable ”. The interpolation is undefined for those masks, so these files carry no tensors. Variables in each file: metricTensor : the tensors at SH order 6 [2×2×793]. familyGram : per-cue-family Gram matrices JᵀJ before noise weighting, at SH orders 4, 6 and 8 [2×2×793×3 families×3 orders]. They let you recompute the tensors with other noise values or SH orders. In reconstruction files only: crossFamilyGram : the unsymmetrised cross terms J_refᵀ J_recon, same layout as familyGram . airmByDirection : the pointwise AIRM discrepancy from the reference. Metadata: coordinates (Cartesian and azimuth/elevation in degrees), cue band, noise values (reference files only), status (“ completed ” or “ not_applicable ”) and, for not-applicable files, a message giving the reason. SHA256SUMS.txt lists a checksum for every file. Format and use The files are MATLAB v7.3 (HDF5), so MATLAB, h5py or any HDF5 reader can open them. Note that h5py reverses MATLAB’s axis order. scripts/fisher_lib.py in the repository reads them and recomputes tensors, AIRM and thresholds from the Gram matrices. To rerun the analysis scripts, unzip into results/evaluation/ so the subject folders sit in results/evaluation/metric_tensors/ . Provenance Produced with run_evaluation("tensors") from the repository above. The values are numerically identical to the tensor files behind results/evaluation/full_evaluation_summary.csv ; this run additionally stores the cross terms. The tensors are derived from the SONICOM HRTF Dataset (Engel et al., J. Audio Eng. Soc. 71(5), 2023, doi:10.17743/jaes.2022.0066). The SONICOM HRTFs are released under the MIT licence. This work develops research begun for the author’s B.Sc. dissertation at Birmingham City University.
title: Fisher information metric tensors for 'Evaluating Spatial Discriminability Preservation in HRTF Upsampling Using Fisher Information'

summary: Code and data of Chapter 3 of the doctoral thesis Mathematical models to describe tumoral behaviors under treatment regimens (Graduate Program in Biometrics, Institute of Biosciences, São Paulo State University, Botucatu, 2026). The deposit covers a three-population ordinary differential equation model of cutaneous melanoma under CAR T-cell therapy with tumor-associated macrophages: its equilibria and local asymptotic stability, the Hopf bifurcation driven by the pro-tumoral action of the macrophages, a variance-based global sensitivity analysis (eFAST), the Bayesian calibration against the immunocompetent B16 data of Jilani et al. (2024), the structural identifiability analysis with StructuralIdentifiability.jl, the profile-likelihood analysis of practical identifiability, the Fisher-information comparison of experimental designs, and the computational scenarios built on the calibrated model. Each folder has a README with its structure, and REPRODUCE.md gives the command that produces each figure and table of the chapter. The MCMC chains are deposited separately because of their size.
title: Melanoma under CAR T-cell therapy with TAM-mediated immunosuppression: model analysis, Bayesian calibration and identifiability (code and data)

summary: Version 3 is an organisational change only: the four subsections of the verification section are reordered so that the two Krook levels, the amplitude equation and the Vlasov solver, precede the two with diffusion and drag, the amplitude equation with diffusion and drag and the Vlasov solver with the Fokker–Planck operator. No text, number, figure or table is changed from version 2, and the description below is version 2’s. Version 2 of this paper adds a related-work section placing the work against the analytic quasi-steady theory of Lestz and Duarte (2021), the regime maps of Zhang et al. (2026) and the steady-or-chirping criterion of Duarte et al. (2017, 2018); places the near-marginal comparison against Lestz and Duarte's two validity constraints and withdraws version 1's reading of the 24 percent gap, which is now a candidate explanation and not an established one; relabels the drag ratio of the ITER-like slice as the collisional ratio of Lilley et al. and places the turbulence-corrected ITER ratio, an order of magnitude smaller, between the two steady slices tested; states the comparison with the cold-background regime map at the point where the reduced model fails; narrows three statements of version 1 to what was tested; and adds the experiments version 1 left open, a reverse ramp pair at the first operating point and the edge and a benchmark pair at a second operating point. An erratum corrects a sentence of version 1's Limits section that had the two near-threshold amplitudes reversed: the held level of the full- f solver is 24 percent above the cubic equation's steady state, not the other way round. The paper builds and verifies a two-level reduced model of a fast-ion-driven mode, the Berk–Breizman bump-on-tail problem, as a plant whose purpose is to locate and characterise the regime in which the mode saturates to a steady state, the regime a fusion power plant must stay in. Level 0 is the near-threshold cubic amplitude equation with Krook, diffusive and drag collisions; Level 1 is a full- f one-dimensional Vlasov solver with a Krook operator; Level 2 adds drag and diffusion acting on the departure from the initial distribution. Each level was verified against the literature before its results were used: the amplitude equation reproduces the critical Krook rate 4.4 and the critical diffusion rate 2.05; the Vlasov solver reproduces the linear growth rate and frequency to 0.01 percent, conserves energy to second order, and reproduces the Berk–Breizman saturation law within 4 percent across the steady region and the diffusive saturation formula within 4 to 7 percent away from marginal stability. For the warm distribution used, the external damping on the field is only 87 percent effective as an amplitude damping, so marginal stability lies at a damping of 1.15 times the collisionless drive rather than 1.0; with that correction the full- f solver agrees with the cubic equation on the steady side of the bifurcation near threshold, and saturates 24 percent above it at a finite distance from marginal stability, in the direction and of the size that other simulations have reported against the same theory. The steady region is mapped in the damping–collision plane: with Krook collisions the oscillating region is a tongue at collision rates below 0.3 to 0.4 of the drive, closed above it; with diffusion equal to the drive, with or without drag at 0.7 of diffusion, every damping from 0.1 to 0.9 of the drive is steady, one point still rising at the end of its run; with drag at 1.2 of diffusion no steady point was found, and at the strongest drives the reduced model leaves its validity where a cold-background resonant model saturates steadily. The edge of the steady region along the collision axis lies between diffusion rates of 0.4 and 0.5 of the drive at a damping of 0.5 of the drive, converged on two velocity grids, and within the same bracket at a damping of 0.3, where every steady level is 1.41
title: A reduced bump-on-tail plant for the steady operating region of a fast-ion-driven mode: amplitude equation, full-f Vlasov solver with Fokker-Planck collisions, regime map and a detection benchmark

summary: This document contains supplemental material of the paper " Global Minima of the Thomson Problem in a Disk: A Molecular Dynamics Approach with Fixed Border Charges ", where the Thomson problem in a disk has been studied. Here we report the lowest minima for the configurations with N = 54 , 60 , 61 , 65 , 66 , 82 , 83 , 85 , 88 , 89 , 90 , 91 , 92 , 97 , 99 , 100 , 101 , 102 , 103 , 104 , 105 , 111 , 113 , 117 , 119 , 133 , 137 , 141 , 149 , 150 , 151 , 153 , 155 , 187 , 286 , and 318 confined particles, obtained by the Quenched Molecular Dynamics (QMD) method. The energy of these configurations is lower than that of the configurations reported by Amore and Zarate ([ Phys. Rev. E. 108 , 055302 (2023) ]; see the supplemental material in Ref. [ 10.5281/zenodo.8301044 ]). For systems with N = 92 , 100 , 102 , 113 , and 133 particles, in contrast to the asymmetric Voronoi diagrams obtained by previous optimization algorithms, our solutions exhibit a clear D1 (axial) symmetry of defects. For a system with N = 286 particles, in contrast to the asymmetric Voronoi diagrams obtained by previous optimization algorithms, our solution exhibits a clear C2  (central inversion) symmetry of defects. However, for a system with N = 150  particles, the lower energy configuration results in a reduction in the symmetry of the defects. Voronoi diagrams are displayed for the 26 configurations that exhibit structural or orientational changes in the defect pattern compared to Ref. [ 10.5281/zenodo.8301044 ], whereas for the remaining 10 systems (with N = 61 , 83 , 85 , 89 , 90 , 91 ,  97 , 99 , 119 , and 137 particles) QMD method refines the equilibrium coordinates and lowers the energy within the same Voronoi topology.
title: Global Minima of the Thomson Problem in a Disk: A Molecular Dynamics Approach with Fixed Border Charges. Supplemental Material

summary: Subclonal reconstruction results produced with CliPP 1.4 for three datasets: 5,424 tumors from TCGA, 2,008 whole-genome tumors from PCAWG, and CliPPSim4k, a cohort of 4,000 simulated tumors with known ground truth. Also deposited are 13,960 TCGA driver mutations annotated with clonality, and the cancer type and tumor purity of every sample in the two real cohorts. These are the files served for download by CliPP-on-Web (https://bioinformatics.mdanderson.org/apps/CliPP/), the web interface to CliPP (https://github.com/wwylab/CliPP). The deposit accompanies manuscript submission and is the stable version as of 16 October 2026. Yujie Jiang and Matthew D. Montierth contributed equally to this work. Wenyi Wang is the corresponding author. README.md describes each archive's layout and the columns of every file.
title: Scalable subclonal reconstruction of cancer cells in DNA sequencing data using a penalized likelihood model

summary: We study the fine phase-space spectral asymptotics of a model class of infinite-order pseudodifferential operators whose symbols grow like exp(c|ξ|^2), c > 0. The leading Weyl law for such operators is known, but the complete logarithmic structure of the heat trace, the singularity structure of the associated zeta function, and the correct notion of a renormalized determinant require a more delicate analysis. We prove that, in dimension four, the reduced heat trace admits the complete asymptotic expansion τ(t) = A L^2 + B L log L + C L + D (log L)^2 + E log L + F + O(1/L), where L = log(1/t), and all coefficients A, B, C, D, E, F are computed explicitly. Consequently, the model zeta function has the structure ζ(s) = α_2 s^(-2) + α_1 (log s)/s + β_1 s^(-1) + γ_2 (log s)^2 + γ_1 log s + ζ_0 + O(s log s) as s → 0^+, with all displayed coefficients determined explicitly. Because the remainder generally produces terms of the form s log s in the renormalized zeta function, the classical derivative ζ'_ren(0) is not automatically finite. We therefore introduce a finite-part renormalized determinant, defined through the constant term in the derivative expansion, and prove its existence under the full asymptotic hierarchy of the heat trace. We also show that in odd dimensions the zeta function possesses algebraic branch points rather than poles, and we explain why the classical zeta determinant construction must be modified. Finally, we recover the growth exponent α from the counting function in the model a(ξ) ∼ exp(c|ξ|^α), and we compare the results with the theories of Pilipović–Prangoski–Vindas, Gilkey–Grubb, Kontsevich–Vishik, and Nicola–Rodino.
title: Fine Structure of Spectral Asymptotics for Infinite-Order Pseudodifferential Operators with Second-Order Exponential Growth

summary: NANOROBOT-ENHANCED DIGITAL TWINS OF BRAIN STATE AT THE LIMIT A multiscale, uncertainty-aware research atlas on microrobotic observations, neural inverse problems, active model discrimination and the limits of computational brain twins. This research monograph asks whether additional microscale observations or strictly bounded reversible experiments can distinguish competing neural-state models that explain conventional measurements equally well. The twin is explicitly defined as a versioned scientific belief, not a digital person, a mind reader or a clinically validated instrument. Its objective is not maximum model complexity but improved identifiability, calibrated prediction under new conditions and faithful retention of failed hypotheses. The work develops five layers: multiscale neural and microenvironment state representation; posterior equivalence and prior sensitivity; non-clinical safe experimental design; frozen-version forking, rollback and reference ancestry; and blind prospective validation against classical state-space systems and independently specified alternatives. Its research architecture includes 30 distinct mathematical derivation plates linked to later chapters, 82 chapters with five independently paginated research sections apiece, 200 detailed Research Gates and 33 revisable Phoenix Answer Embryos. A DOI evidence ledger identifies existing support for brain modeling, latent neural dynamics, experiment design and preclinical microrobot tracking while preventing those sources from being mistaken for evidence of the proposed integrated system. Key research questions include: Can two equally accurate virtual brains be separated by a small, permissible observation? How can the effect of a measurement itself be separated from neural change? When does a prior dominate the inferred brain state? Can the model predict unseen function rather than reconstruct a training signal? Can another laboratory reproduce a rejected twin and safely return to an earlier version? SCIENTIFIC STATUS AND LIMITATIONS This is a forward-looking, non-clinical research synthesis and experimental hypothesis architecture. It provides no personal medical advice, patient-specific interpretations or instruction to deliver neural interventions. Existing murine microrobot tracking and virtual-brain modeling studies do not establish autonomous neural nanorobot readout, human safety, privacy-sensitive mind inference or therapeutic efficacy. Proposed formulas, experiments, research gates and answer embryos are not newly validated biological laws or executed experiments. The work keeps independent safety vetoes, privacy, external reproducibility and explicit model retirement as first-class constraints. Research questions remain open to refutation, correction and reconstruction by future human and AI researchers.

summary: This replication package accompanies the paper "An Exploratory Evaluation of Targeted Label Poisoning in a Client-Local Feature Federated Ensemble for Chest X-Ray Classification." It contains code and saved experimental results for an exploratory study of Pneumonia-to-Normal label poisoning in four-class chest X-ray classification. The study uses 20,795 images from three public sources, with 20,557 perceptual groups kept intact across experimental partitions. The package covers 212 completed training jobs, including main and component comparisons, classifier-head sensitivity, image-model references, candidate probability banks, and earlier-poisoning experiments. The main comparisons and image-model references use ten deterministic seeds. The classifier-head and GRU-structure study uses three seeds. Included materials comprise dataset manifests and image checksums, perceptual-group metadata, split assignments, seeds and configurations, held-out predictions, candidate probabilities, numerical summaries, result figures, analysis and verification scripts, and scientific execution-source snapshots. Additional fixed-model analyses examine validation availability, validation-label contamination, and artifact retention. The README and reproducibility guide explain verification, reanalysis, environment requirements, and dataset reconstruction. Dataset images and model checkpoints are not included. Obtain the source images separately under their applicable access and use terms: COVID-19 Radiography Database: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/tawsifurrahman/covid19-radiography-database COVID19, Pneumonia, Normal Chest X-ray Images: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/sachinkumar413/covid-pneumonia-normal-chest-xray-images Tuberculosis Chest X-ray Dataset: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/tawsifurrahman/tuberculosis-tb-chest-xray-dataset The included metadata identify the exact study images for reconstruction from the original source bytes. Saved results can be checked without source images or retraining. The attack direction was selected exploratorily, perceptual grouping does not establish patient independence, and source-held-out generalization was not evaluated. Reuse rights are described in LICENSE_STATUS.txt. This work was supported by the Deanship of Scientific Research (DSR) at King Abdulaziz University, Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, under grant No. IPP: 455-611-2026.
title: Replication Package for: An Exploratory Evaluation of Targeted Label Poisoning in a Client-Local Feature Federated Ensemble for Chest X-Ray Classification

summary: Blind Source Separation(BSS) is a fundamental problem in signal processing, aiming to separate multiple source signals from their mixtures without prior knowledge of the sources or the mixing process. Traditional approaches, such as Independent Vector Analysis (IVA) exploits statistical independence of sources. Recently, diffusion-based approaches have emerged as a promising alternative by leveraging powerful generative priors. Among them, ArrayDPS formulates BSS problem as a posterior sampling problem, and utilizes a pretrained speech diffusion model to guide the recovery of clean source signals. A key factor behind its separation capability is the multi-channel consistency (MC) objective, which enforces the estimated source signals to reconstruct the observed microphone mixtures through the estimated acoustic transfer functions. However, the number of microphones in the array is often limited, which constrains the performance of ArrayDPS. To address this issue, we propose VM-ArrayDPS, a novel method that augments the microphone array with virtual microphones with higher-SNR, these microphones can offer extra MC constraints to enhance the separation performance. Experimental results demonstrate that VM-ArrayDPS significantly outperforms ArrayDPS on both 2-speaker and 3-speaker datasets, showcasing the effectiveness of virtual microphone augmentation in improving BSS performance. We also did ablation studies to show the influence of the number of virtual microphones and weight of the MC objective brought by virtual microphones.
title: VM-ARRAYDPS: Virtual Microphone Augmented Diffusion Posterior Sampling for Unsupervised Blind Speech Separation

summary: Although room impulse responses (RIRs) encode source-distance cues, conventional monaural source separation focuses on recovering audio content without estimating source-specific RIRs, losing the associated spatial information. To address this limitation, we propose Distance-Aware Monaural Source Separation using Multi-RIR Estimation (DAMSEP), the first end-to-end framework that is jointly trained for source separation and multi-source RIR estimation from a single-microphone mixture. DAMSEP integrates a separation backbone with shared dereverberation and RIR estimation modules to jointly recover clean sources and source-specific complex convolutive transfer functions under source estimation and reverberant reconstruction objectives, enabling relative near/far ordering through the direct-to-reverberant ratios of the corresponding RIRs. For comprehensive evaluation, we introduce HETMIXR, which spans heterogeneous source content and diverse simulated room conditions with source-specific RIRs and geometric distance annotations. Experiments on HETMIXR demonstrate superior performance in source separation, RIR estimation, and distance ordering. Ablation studies reveal the complementary benefits of source supervision and reverberant reconstruction, while additional evaluations show generalization to single-speaker inputs and mixtures generated using measured RIRs from an unseen room. Our code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Wenanzhi/DAMSEP.
title: DAMSEP: Distance-Aware Monaural Source Separation using Multi-RIR Estimation

summary: Discrete audio tokenization has become the critical interface between raw waveforms and autoregressive modeling in recent music generation. As a result, music tokenizers must simultaneously support high-fidelity reconstruction and produce discrete sequences that remain amenable to language modeling. Existing reconstruction-oriented tokenizers often mix musical structure with fine acoustic details, producing high-entropy tokens that are hard to model. In contrast, semantics-guided alternatives are designed for speech and do not fit music well, often hurting reconstruction quality. We address these trade-offs by rethinking music tokenization around a measurable notion of music semantic content grounded in downstream Music Information Retrieval tasks. Guided by this definition, we propose MuSeC, a music semantic codec that factorizes semantic and acoustic content directly from mixed signals without source separation. MuSeC preserves information required for high-fidelity reconstruction while producing more LM-friendly discrete units. Empirically, it improves reconstruction quality and yields more predictable token sequences, providing a practical foundation toward high-fidelity LLM music generation. Demos are available at https://longwaytog0.github.io/MuSeC/.
title: Rethinking Music Tokenization: A Semantic Codec toward High-Fidelity LLM Music Generation

summary: We present DECAF, a privacy preserving neural speech codec that obfuscates a speaker's voice while preserving linguistic content while maintaining automatic speech recognition (ASR) performance at very low bitrates, inspired by decaffeination. At the transmitter end, speech is encoded into speaker independent content embeddings, which are compressed using residual vector quantization and transmitted without any speaker related information. At the receiver, a canonical speaker embedding, shared a priori between endpoints, is used for waveform reconstruction, enabling deterministic and consistent obfuscation of a speaker's voice. The proposed framework leverages an information bottleneck applied to self supervised representations, along with a separate speaker embedding branch, to achieve effective speaker content disentanglement. We further incorporate a CTC-based auxiliary objective, encouraging content representations that are well aligned with downstream ASR tasks. We show that DECAF operating at a bit rate of 0.5 kbps achieves an Equal Error Rate (EER) of up to 43.5% for a speaker verification system, while maintaining competitive ASR performance, yielding a relative reduction in word error rate of 33.2% compared to a state of the art method.
title: Decaf: A privacy preserving speech codec using speaker disentanglement and canonical voice conversion

summary: Full-duplex speech models require training data that preserves turn-taking, overlap, interruption, and backchannel behavior, yet these signals are entangled across speakers in noisy real-world recordings. We present Conversational Voice, a pipeline that converts real two-speaker excerpts into three complementary training-data artifacts. (1) Separation recovers speaker-specific tracks with stable speaker assignments, a canonical transcript, and naturally observed interaction timing. (2) Reconstruction generates speech in matched voices from a fixed source transcript, reconstructs the source turn order, pauses, and overlaps, and adds word-level alignment and delivery instructions. (3) Expansion generates new dialogue constrained by the source context, speakers, and observed interaction pattern. Automatic speaker-verification metrics remain strong across stages, with same-speaker similarity of 0.983-0.991 and positive discrimination margins of 0.199-0.209. Predicted speech quality (NISQA MOS) is 3.56 for separation, 4.41 for reconstruction, and 4.61 for expansion. A Gemini-based automatic evaluator assigns expansion mean scores of 4.94/5 for contextual coherence and 4.80/5 for dialogue naturalness. Expansion and reconstruction exhibit broadly similar interaction profiles; expansion's turn, overlap-event, backchannel, and interruption rates are 4.6%, 8.0%, 13.2%, and 16.0% lower, respectively. We evaluate data properties only; downstream gains in full-duplex model training remain for future work.
title: ConversationalVoice: Full-Duplex Speech Data from Real Conversations through Source-Faithful Reconstruction and Conversation-Grounded Expansion

summary: Automatic Drum Transcription (ADT) is commonly formulated as a direct mapping from a music mixture to symbolic drum events. While effective for transcription, this formulation discards the acoustic stems that are useful for editing, remixing, and production. We revisit an alternative separate-and-detect formulation, where a drum source separation front end first produces five editable drum stems, and a fixed onset detector then converts each stem into symbolic events. The separator is built on a five-stem latent diffusion model that jointly generates kick, snare, toms, hi-hats, and cymbals in a compact VAE latent space. We further study two training-only auxiliary branches--an onset branch (OB) and a timbre branch (TB)--which shape the separator during learning but are discarded at inference. Trained on synthetic drum multitracks and evaluated on MDB Drums and ENST-Drums, the proposed pipeline consistently improves over a strong U-Net-based drum separation baseline in overall transcription F1. It also outperforms a representative end-to-end ADT system on kick and snare F1 under our evaluation protocol, while additionally providing separated audio stems. The ablation results show that OB gives the most stable transcription gains, whereas TB changes the trade-off between reconstruction, acoustic stem quality, and onset detection. These results suggest that generative drum demixing can serve not only as a source separation model, but also as a practical front end for interpretable drum transcription.
title: Separate-and-Detect: Unified Drum Transcription and Stem Generation via Latent Diffusion

summary: Acoustic-to-Articulatory Inversion (AAI) estimates vocal tract articulator movements from speech, benefiting tasks like ASR, speech synthesis, and speaker verification. While deep learning-based methods (CNNs, RNNs, Transformers) have advanced AAI, recent studies show that Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) features further enhance performance, particularly in low-resource settings. However, SSL feature extractors introduce inference latency and computational overhead. To address this, we propose a novel pretraining method leveraging three target representations-Phoneme Labels, Articulatory Feature Labels, and Critical-articulator Labels-eliminating the need for an SSL extractor during inference. We evaluate our approach against both baseline and SSL-based models across various data conditions. Results demonstrate that our method consistently improves AAI performance, particularly in low-resource scenarios, while significantly reducing inference costs without sacrificing accuracy.
title: Enhancing Acoustic-to-Articulatory Inversion with Multi-Target Pretraining for Low-Resource Settings

summary: Modern automatic speaker verification (ASV) systems are vulnerable to adversarial perturbations. Diffusion-based purification has recently shown strong effectiveness against such perturbations, but its reverse denoising process requires iterative sampling and leads to high inference latency. We find that the forward noising process provides most of the robustness gain. Motivated by this observation, we reformulate adversarial purification as a learnable noising problem, and propose the Positive-Incentive Noise Predictor (PnP), the first framework that explicitly introduces positive-incentive noise (π-noise) into the purification task. PnP learns input-adaptive π-noise and mixes it with the input to improve the robustness of downstream ASV systems. Experiments on four advanced ASV backbones show that PnP effectively defends against adversarial attacks while preserving performance on natural speech. Compared with representative purification baselines, the proposed framework provides a competitive balance among defense effectiveness, impact on genuine utterances, and inference efficiency under white-box, black-box, and defender-aware adaptive attacks, with a real-time factor as low as 0.014. Moreover, PnP can be cascaded with a diffusion denoiser to further improve the perceptual quality of purified utterances. Code and purified audio examples are available at https://eurecom-asp.github.io/pnp/
title: Positive-Incentive Noise Predictor for Adversarial Purification in Speaker Verification

summary: Distributed microphone arrays composed of multiple subarrays enable blind source separation over a wide spatial area. Directly applying fast multichannel nonnegative matrix factorization (FastMNMF) to all subarrays can exploit observations from all subarrays, but it requires repeated inversions of large matrices spanning all microphones, causing the computational cost to increase rapidly as the number of microphones grows. In contrast, applying FastMNMF to one subarray reduces the matrix size but cannot exploit observations from other subarrays. We propose distributed FastMNMF, which imposes a block-diagonal structure on the source spatial covariance matrices, so that matrix inversions are performed within subarrays. The NMF-based source spectrogram model is shared across subarrays, allowing the method to aggregate source activity information while discarding inter-subarray covariance. In synchronized, noiseless simulations with fixed room and array/source geometry, the method required less computation time than conventional FastMNMF using all subarrays, achieved a higher average source-to-distortion ratio than conventional FastMNMF using one subarray, and was applicable in the tested five-source condition, where each four-microphone subarray was locally underdetermined.
title: Fast Multichannel NMF with Block-Diagonal Spatial Covariance Matrices for Efficient Blind Source Separation Using Distributed Microphone Arrays

summary: Automatic speaker verification (ASV) systems are highly vulnerable to presentation attacks, also called spoofing attacks. Replay is among the simplest attacks to mount - yet difficult to detect reliably. The generalization failure of spoofing countermeasures (CMs) has driven the community to study various alternative deep learning CMs. The majority of them are supervised approaches that learn a human-spoof discriminator. In this paper, we advocate a different, deep generative approach that leverages from powerful unsupervised manifold learning in classification. The potential benefits include the possibility to sample new data, and to obtain insights to the latent features of genuine and spoofed speech. To this end, we propose to use variational autoencoders (VAEs) as an alternative backend for replay attack detection, via three alternative models that differ in their class-conditioning. The first one, similar to the use of Gaussian mixture models (GMMs) in spoof detection, is to train independently two VAEs - one for each class. The second one is to train a single conditional model (C-VAE) by injecting a one-hot class label vector to the encoder and decoder networks. Our final proposal integrates an auxiliary classifier to guide the learning of the latent space. Our experimental results using constant-Q cepstral coefficient (CQCC) features on the ASVspoof 2017 and 2019 physical access subtask datasets indicate that the C-VAE offers substantial improvement in comparison to training two separate VAEs for each class. On the 2019 dataset, the C-VAE outperforms the VAE and the baseline GMM by an absolute 9 - 10% in both equal error rate (EER) and tandem detection cost function (t-DCF) metrics. Finally, we propose VAE residuals - the absolute difference of the original input and the reconstruction as features for spoofing detection.
title: Deep Generative Variational Autoencoding for Replay Spoof Detection in Automatic Speaker Verification

summary: We develop a rigorous finite-dimensional mathematical framework connecting the renormalization group, gradient flows, Lyapunov stability, and noncooperative game theory. The central object is a renormalization-group flow written in gradient form, dg_i/dt = β_i(g) = - ∑_j G_ij(g) ∂Γ/∂g_j(g),          (1) where g = (g_1, …, g_n) belongs to an open domain M ⊂ ℝⁿ, Γ is a C² function, and G(g) is a symmetric positive-definite matrix. We associate to this flow a common-payoff game whose payoff is U(g) = - Γ(g).                   (2) We prove, with complete arguments, that ordinary Nash equilibria always imply renormalization-group fixed points, but the converse is false. We then identify the exact condition under which a fixed point becomes a genuine stable equilibrium of the game: a nondegenerate renormalization-group fixed point is asymptotically stable if and only if the Hessian of Γ is positive definite, if and only if it is a strict local minimum of Γ, if and only if it is a strict strong Nash equilibrium of U = -Γ. The distinction between ordinary Nash equilibrium and strong Nash equilibrium is essential. Ordinary Nash equilibria allow only unilateral deviations, while strong Nash equilibria exclude all small joint deviations. We provide explicit counterexamples showing that fixed points need not be Nash equilibria, that ordinary Nash equilibria need not be stable, and that invertibility of G alone does not imply finiteness of equilibria. We also prove global existence results under compactness and finiteness results under Morse nondegeneracy. The paper is self-contained at the level of multivariable calculus, linear algebra, ordinary differential equations, and basic Lyapunov stability theory. The framework is intentionally conditional: it does not claim that the gradient-flow representation has been proven in four-dimensional QCD or in any specific quantum field theory. Those issues are placed in a final section of open problems.
title: Gradient-Flow Renormalization Group as a Common-Potential Game: A Rigorous Equivalence Between Asymptotically Stable Fixed Points and Strict Strong Nash Equilibria

summary: International business (IB) theory explains how firms enter foreign markets, allocate ownership, govern cross-border activities, build networks, and accumulate market knowledge. Less explicit attention has been given to the internationalization of the firm’s continuing operating system itself. This article develops the concept of operational internationalization: the cross-border extension of recurring fulfilment, inventory, logistics, service, compliance, and information processes, regardless of whether the underlying capabilities are fully owned by the focal firm. It further introduces operational embeddedness and boundary asymmetry to explain why ownership, governance, operational, and jurisdictional boundaries may overlap without expanding synchronously. Sovereign jurisdiction is treated as a constitutive boundary because tax, customs, data, product, environmental, and related rules shape which cross-border configurations are institutionally admissible. The framework becomes dynamic through reverse value-information flow, whereby economically consequential market and jurisdictional information generated abroad enters subsequent production, allocation, service, and organizational decisions. Just-in-Place (JIP) is positioned within this architecture as the enactment logic through which geographically and institutionally dispersed capabilities are selectively activated and recombined. A comparative public-disclosure analysis of Linamar and JD Logistics provides complementary evidence of inward informational feedback and outward operational extension. The article reconceptualizes internationalization as a reflexive, multi-boundary process in which the operating system itself becomes an analytically distinct object of cross-border expansion.
title: Internationalizing the Operating System: Operational Embeddedness, Jurisdictional Boundaries, and Just-in-Place

summary: No contexto atual de valorização das práticas sustentáveis e da eficiência operacional, a logística reversa apresenta-se como uma ferramenta estratégica na gestão de resíduos sólidos em ambientes aeroportuários. O presente estudo tem como objetivo analisar os principais desafios relacionados à logística reversa no Aeroporto Internacional de São Paulo/Guarulhos, bem como avaliar o uso de tecnologias aplicadas à logística como forma de otimização dos processos. A metodologia adotada baseia-se em revisão bibliográfica e análise de estudos de caso. Os resultados demonstram que a ausência de um sistema integrado de gestão de resíduos, aliada à baixa utilização de tecnologias, compromete a eficiência operacional e gera perdas financeiras. Como proposta, sugere-se a implantação de um sistema inteligente de monitoramento de resíduos com uso de Internet das Coisas (IoT), visando aumentar a eficiência da coleta seletiva e o reaproveitamento de materiais.
title: Logística Reversa e Tecnologia Aplicada no Aeroporto Internacional de Guarulhos: Desafios e Soluções Operacionais

summary: We study diagonal infinite-order operators on the flat torus of the form P = A(|D|),                        (1) where D = -i∇ is the momentum operator on T^n and A: [0,∞) → (0,∞) is a positive radial symbol with super-polynomial growth. Under explicit log-convexity and steepness assumptions on A, we prove a Weyl law for the eigenvalue counting function, a leading heat-kernel asymptotic, and the small positive-s behavior of the spectral zeta function. The main proved results are the following. 1. Weyl law with an elementary remainder: N_P(λ) = C_n (A^(-1)(λ))^n + O((A^(-1)(λ))^(n-1)), λ → ∞,                                 (2) where C_n = ω_n/(2π)^n, ω_n = π^(n/2)/Γ(n/2 + 1).           (3) 2. Leading heat-kernel asymptotic: Tr(e^(-tP)) = C_n (R(t))^n (1 + o(1)), t → 0+,           (4) where R(t) is defined by A(R(t)) = 1/t.                    (5) 3. Zeta asymptotics in terms of the inverse growth function. Define G(u) = (A^(-1)(e^u))^n.  (6) Assume that, as u → ∞, G(u) ~ u^ρ L(u), where ρ ≥ 0 and L is slowly varying. If ρ = 0, assume also that G(u) → ∞. Then, as s → 0+, ζ_P(s) ~ C_n Γ(ρ + 1) s^(-ρ) L(1/s). 4. For the model symbols A(r) = exp(l r^q), l > 0, q ≥ 1,                                       (7) and, more generally, A(r) = exp^(k)(l r^q), k ≥ 2, l > 0, q > 0, we obtain explicit asymptotics. If d = n/q, then:                                  (8) For depth k = 1:               (9) N_P(λ) ~ C_n l^(-d) (log λ)^d, Tr(e^(-tP)) ~ C_n l^(-d) (log(1/t))^d, ζ_P(s) ~ C_n l^(-d) Γ(d + 1) s^(-d). For depth k ≥ 2: N_P(λ) ~ C_n l^(-d) (log^(k) λ)^d, Tr(e^(-tP)) ~ C_n l^(-d) (log^(k)(1/t))^d, ζ_P(s) ~ C_n l^(-d) (log^(k-1)(1/s))^d. Here exp^(1)(x) = e^x, exp^(k+1)(x) = exp(exp^(k)(x)), log^(1)(x) = log x, and log^(k+1)(x) = log(log^(k)(x)). The paper proves only statements that are fully justified in the diagonal commutative model. Noncommutative residue theory, decomposition assumptions, spectral triples, local residue pairing formulas, integrality statements, and topological residue theorems are not proved here and are listed as open problems.
title: HEAT KERNEL, WEYL LAW, AND ZETA ASYMPTOTICS FOR DIAGONAL INFINITE-ORDER OPERATORS WITH SUPER-POLYNOMIAL GROWTH

summary: Code, trained weights and campaign results for the paper "Morphological diffusion by ball births: generative models of binary images with exact Betti increments" by M. Zéraï, submitted to the Journal of Mathematical Imaging and Vision. The model generates binary images by births of maximal balls. Its forward process is a random granulometry, and its reverse process learns a birth map. morpho_repro.tar.gz contains the implementation (model, sampler, exact Euler increments, measurement protocol), the averaged (EMA) weights of all trained models on the three datasets (GRF, BBBC039 nuclei masks, MNIST), the campaign reports and logs, and the GRF data. README.md gives the hyperparameters, the source of each table and the reproduction commands. figs_print.tar.gz contains the figure boards of the paper with their statistics. The BBBC039 masks and MNIST are public and are downloaded by prepare_data.sh. Note: the two archives are gzip-compressed tar files, deposited as morpho_repro.tar and figs_print.tar (README.md names them morpho_repro.tar.gz and figs_print.tar.gz). Extract them with: tar xzf morpho_repro.tar
title: Morphological diffusion by ball births: code, trained weights and campaign results

summary: Hashing, signing, and timestamping establish that a document has not changed. When a legal document is produced by composition, from templates, clause libraries, shared definitions, and parameters that evolve independently, the governing text is a resolved state, and the integrity of the root document does not ensure that this state can be reconstructed. We treat this as a problem of ex post auditability. We define the resolved state as S_t = ρ(A_0, R_t, C_t), derive five properties of its auditability from requirements established in archival science, legal document standards, and norm-change formalisms, and introduce a capture model K_t with a diagnostic procedure that reports which properties a capture fails. We implement the framework in cmacc-attest and apply it to the 175 instantiated contracts of the CommonAccord library. References resolve in 96.6% of contracts, yet none is auditable: no reference is version-locked, and 98.3% contain conflicts settled by an unattested precedence order. Replaying 194 commits of the library history shows that 88.5% of the changes in resolved contracts left the root file unchanged. Repository history narrows reconstruction when the time of resolution is known, but does not replace a capture.
title: Beyond Document Integrity: Auditing Resolved States of Formalized Legal Documents

summary: MULTI-AGENT ROUTING OF NEUROVASCULAR MICROROBOT SWARMS AT THE LIMIT This research monograph develops a falsifiable, non-clinical framework for routing heterogeneous microrobotic teams through branching neurovascular vessel phantoms. It asks whether decentralized task assignment, flow-aware navigation, independently tracked agent identity, and verifiable recovery can improve qualified sensing or inert-sample collection without increasing collision, occlusion, flow disturbance, thermal burden, sample confusion, or residual material risk. Organized around low-Reynolds-number hydrodynamics, multi-agent coordination, and independently enforced physical safety boundaries, the volume contains 30 mathematical derivation plates, 82 full research chapters with five separately paginated sections each, 200 detailed Research Gates, and 33 provisional Phoenix Answer Embryos. A DOI evidence ledger distinguishes established component physics and published demonstrations from the original system-level hypotheses proposed here. Strong passive-transport, single-agent, and information-matched centralized alternatives remain valid competitors throughout. Research failures, abandoned models, experimental uncertainty, and successor reconstruction are treated as scientific outputs, not editorial defects. The monograph provides a research architecture and prospective tests, not results from experiments performed for this publication. It does not assert demonstrated autonomous navigation in human cerebral vessels, clinical safety, therapeutic efficacy, or authorization for human intervention.

summary: Unrefereed AI-assisted mathematical candidate for the iid prophet inequality over time with arbitrary lease durations. summary: Every element of the causal chain that produced the five largest mass extinctions of the last half-billion years is presently accelerating in the Earth system. The rate of the modern perturbation exceeds every peer-reviewed paleoclimate reference case. A six-intervention portfolio, deployed together at wartime industrial scale beginning now, is the physically necessary and sufficient response. The window in which that portfolio remains fully effective closes between 2028 and 2040. The anthropogenic-versus-feedback tipping point is expected between 2035 and 2040; corrected for the at-least-order-of-magnitude higher rate of contemporary carbon release, loss of agency — the point at which coordinated intervention can no longer arrest the cascade — arrives 200 to 400 years after feedback engagement under sustained portfolio deployment, and collapses onto the tipping point itself under any scenario in which the portfolio is not deployed within the 2028–2040 window. Background. The five largest mass-extinction events of the Phanerozoic share a consistent causal chain: rapid carbon injection to the ocean-atmosphere system, followed by warming, ocean deoxygenation, acidification, and preferential loss of marine calcifiers, with multi-million-year recovery for reef ecosystems. Every element of that chain is presently active and gaining speed. The current anthropogenic perturbation is capable of driving a combination and magnitude of ocean geochemical changes unparalleled in the geological record reviewed by Hönisch et al. (2012), which covers approximately the past 300 million years. The reef–ocean-oxygen–land coupling documented in the End-Permian record demonstrates that marine biosphere collapse propagates to terrestrial extinction through the shared oxygen and biogeochemical infrastructure of the coupled Earth system; contemporary marine indicators are therefore leading indicators of terrestrial as well as marine risk. Approach. This three-part synthesis compiles peer-reviewed reconstructions of the Big Five causal chain, measures each element against the contemporary Earth system using the most recent authoritative data (Friedlingstein et al. 2026; Wu et al. 2021; Zeebe et al. 2016; Hönisch et al. 2012; Schmidtko et al. 2017; Eddy et al. 2021; Spady et al. 2026), specifies the physically necessary intervention portfolio, and characterizes the near-term feedback, resource, and civilizational risk environment those interventions must succeed in. Part I establishes the paleoclimate analog. Part II specifies the intervention portfolio. Part III maps the contemporary Earth system the Part II portfolio must succeed in — which climate feedbacks are already engaged and how they cascade, which physical resources are hitting hard limits inside the same two-to-three-decade window, and how those pressures translate into food, water, migration, health, economic, and governance strain — and closes with the North American Climate Pain Scale (NAPS), a 1–10 diagnostic instrument that anchors climate severity to concrete events so policymakers and the public can locate today's conditions and the trajectory ahead. Findings. Every element of the paleoclimate extinction causal chain is presently active. Atmospheric CO₂ (422.8 ppm, 2024 global annual mean; Friedlingstein et al. 2026) has exceeded the reconstructed latest-Permian baseline of 426 (+133 / −96) ppm (Wu et al. 2021, Nature Communications). summary: This reproducibility archive accompanies Marco Mantovanelli's A Multi-Arch Perturbed Hofstadter Q-Recursion: Gaussian Profiles and Exact Frequency Laws. It contains the manuscript PDF, complete LaTeX source, six vector figures, independent verification programs, figure-generation code, numerical reports, and sampled figure data. The paper studies Q(n) = Q(n - Q(n-1)) + Q(n - Q(n-2)) - (-1)^n for n >= 8, with the seven prescribed initial values (1, 1, 3, 3, 3, 3, 5). A causal binary-word construction proves global existence and an exact factorization into three signed excursions. Their uniformly convergent Gaussian profiles explain three limiting sign transitions per standard dyadic block and a sharp normalized error envelope of approximately 0.067088003576. The paper also proves exact finite transition locations, an ordered frequency factorization, a shifted 2-adic valuation law on pure dyadic value blocks, and a summatory asymptotic with an explicit continuous periodic term. The archived verification compares all 33,554,432 directly computed terms with an independent word reconstruction, checks complete frequency blocks through level 21, and verifies the exact summatory identity at every even cutoff from 8 through 33,554,432. Separate programs audit the word maps, finite transitions, and exact two-head identities. These computations supplement the general proofs in the manuscript. The original perturbation, OEIS A394051, is discussed for comparison.
title: A Multi-Arch Perturbed Hofstadter Q-Recursion: Gaussian Profiles and Exact Frequency Laws (Reproducibility Archive)

summary: This paper offers a candidate descriptive model based on the author’s retrospective account of internal agent-like experience during a past period of social isolation, emotional distress and perceived high cognitive load. It is a non-clinical reconstruction, not a technique, treatment or recommendation. No contemporaneous physiological, behavioral or neuroimaging measurements were recorded. The Opposition–Load–Coupling vocabulary organizes reported phases of self-talk, opposition, felt load, perceived coupling, autonomy, boundary degradation and disengagement. These are reported experiences and interpretive constructs, not demonstrated causal mechanisms. Claimed benefits and harms are unmeasured first-person reports. The Shared Value Anchor is an untested candidate predictor, not an established stabilizer or necessary condition. The case does not establish whether value conflict preceded initial boundary degradation or distinguish the proposal from a simpler load-based account. The model is situated alongside dialogical-self, Internal Family Systems, predictive-processing, imaginary-companion, writer-agency and tulpa literature. Any incremental contribution lies in the proposed coupling vocabulary and separately testable value-anchor hypothesis, not in discovering internal multiplicity or proving a new mechanism. Safety: do not intentionally induce or replicate the conditions described. This is the author’s own past experience, published at the author’s direction; no formal ethics approval or exemption is claimed. Version 4 incorporates author-adopted revisions following advisory and changed-text checks, including prior-involved AI reviewers. Those checks are not independent peer review, clinical validation or evidence of effectiveness.

summary: Four-dimensional beam-matrix reconstruction from quadrupole scans is the standard way to mea- sure cross-plane coupling and the intrinsic emittances that a decoupling section can recover. We show that a scan of a single thin quadrupole, normal or skew and placed anywhere in a linear lattice, determines at most nine of the ten beam-matrix parameters for any number of settings, because each measured second moment is quadratic in the quadrupole strength. The unmeasured direction lies in the x–y cross block and has a closed form in terms of the transfer matrices; for a quadrupole followed by a drift of length L its nonzero entries are Wxpy = Wpxy = 1 and Wpxpy = −2/L. Both projected emittances are therefore measured, but the beam matrices consistent with the data form a line segment along which the smaller intrinsic emittance ranges from zero to slightly above its true value, so a single-knob scan gives only an upper bound on it. A thick quadrupole restores the miss- ing direction only weakly, its singular value scaling approximately as the sixth power of the magnet length. Scanning two independently powered quadrupoles of any type makes the reconstruction well posed without additional hardware.
title: Single-knob quadrupole scans do not determine the intrinsic emittances

summary: Description This dataset accompanies a comparative evolutionary-genomics study of ancestral cytosine substitution patterns across human, chimpanzee, bonobo and gorilla lineages. Using hg38-centered UCSC multiz primate alignments and a seven-species phylogenetic framework, we reconstructed ancestral nucleotide states and quantified cytosine substitutions across all 22 human autosomes. The analysis examined CG, CHG and CHH sequence contexts, 256 strand-canonicalized ancestral 5-mer motifs, and lineage-specific substitution patterns. The deposited files include: Chromosome-level ancestral-site datasets at a minimum ancestral-state posterior probability of 0.95. Chromosome-specific 5-mer substitution summaries and quality-control records. Genome-wide cytosine substitution frequencies and context-enrichment ratios. Chromosome-bootstrap uncertainty estimates and cross-lineage motif comparisons. Statistical analyses of lineage-specific motif deviations, including simultaneous confidence intervals. Leave-one-autosome-out predictive comparisons of ancestral 3-mer and 5-mer sequence context. Frozen methodology documentation, validation records, checksums and the fixed seven-species phylogenetic tree. The dataset supports independent examination and downstream reanalysis of the reported numerical findings. Data provenance: UCSC Genome Browser hg38-centered 30-primate multiz alignments, restricted to seven primate species. Computational methods: IQ-TREE 2.3.6 ancestral-state reconstruction under GTR+F+G4, followed by custom Python-based sequence-context and statistical analyses. Limitations: The archive contains processed ancestral-site data and numerical outputs, not the original complete multiple-sequence alignments. It does not contain ancestral DNA methylation measurements, direct estimates of net CpG gain or loss, or calibrated mutation rates. Associated code: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23425960 Archive organization: This dataset is distributed across two Zenodo records. This record contains Part 1 of 2. Part 2 is available at https://zenodo.org/records/23442145 . Both parts are required to reconstruct the complete archive. Download all files from both records and follow the instructions in RECONSTRUCTION.txt to assemble and verify the dataset.
title: Ancestral Cytosine Sequence-Context Substitution Data Across Four Hominid Lineages: A 22-Autosome Comparative Analysis. Part 1

summary: The rapid expansion of the gig economy, facilitated by digital talent platforms, has fundamentally reconfigured the nature of work, employment relationships, and organizational structures. This paradigm shift from stable, long-term employment to a fluid workforce of contractors, freelancers, and project-based talent presents profound challenges to conventional leadership theories and practices. Traditional models, predicated on hierarchical authority, stable organizational boundaries, and enduring psychological contracts, are proving increasingly inadequate for orchestrating a workforce characterized by autonomy, transience, and distributed networks. This paper conducts a critical review of existing leadership literature—including transformational, adaptive, and emerging platform leadership theories—assessing their applicability and limitations in the gig context. Synthesizing insights from organizational behavior, strategic management, and technology studies, we propose a novel integrated framework: the Fluid Leadership Ecosystem (FLE) Model. The FLE model conceptualizes leadership not as a function of individual authority but as the cultivation of a dynamic ecosystem across three core dimensions: Relational Architecture, Algorithmic Stewardship, and Capability Cultivation. We argue that effective leadership in this new era requires designing trust-enabling infrastructures, ensuring human-centric governance of management algorithms, and fostering portable skill development for a transient workforce. This paper introduces novel theoretical perspectives, including temporal leadership dynamics, polycontextual leadership challenges, and the concept of reverse leadership flows from workers to platforms. By presenting a comprehensive model supported by data visualizations and identifying avenues for empirical validation, this research offers a forward-looking agenda for both scholars and practitioners navigating the complexities of leadership in the 21st-century workforce.
title: The Gig Economy and Talent Platforms: New Models of Leadership for Managing a Fluid Workforce

summary: LONGITUDINAL DEVICE MIGRATION AND MEANING CONTINUITY AT THE LIMIT Device Replacement × Model Bridging × Control Semantics STARLI RESEARCH WORKS | INSTITUTE XXIV | FLAGSHIP 24 Feng Cheng-en 33 × Starli Research Works This research monograph investigates a deceptively difficult question in long-term brain–computer interfaces: when sensors, acquisition electronics, firmware, electrode geometry, or decoding models change, what would justify the claim that a user's task-grounded control meaning has been preserved? Numerical signal alignment alone cannot establish continuity of intention. Two systems may encode different signals while supporting the same functional command, or produce nearly identical latent representations while mapping to incompatible actions. The volume formulates meaning continuity as a conditional, falsifiable engineering and scientific hypothesis. It connects device-specific observation models, neural recording instability, task and action ontologies, paired old/new sensing periods, latent manifold bridging, longitudinal recalibration, calibrated abstention, functional validation, and an accessible right to reject the proposed migration. Its central commitment is that no amount of predictive accuracy can compensate for invalid authorization, an unverified physical reference, or loss of independent control. The research atlas comprises thirty connected mathematical derivations, eighty-two research chapters, and 410 independently paginated chapter sections that examine observables, inverse explanations, discriminating experiments, uncertainty and noncompensable safeguards, and independent requalification. Two hundred detailed Research Gates propose future falsification and handoff programs, while thirty-three Phoenix Answer Embryos preserve revisable candidate approaches rather than immutable conclusions. A claim-scoped DOI evidence ledger connects the study to published work on neural recording drift, decoder adaptation, manifold alignment, longitudinal neural interfaces, speech BCIs, user preferences, and neurotechnology ethics. The book is designed for both human researchers and future AI research systems. Its formulas, chapter cross-links, DOI anchors, competing models, negative-result requirements, and successor-focused research cards provide structured entry points for independent reconstruction and informed disagreement. The visual presentation combines ivory pages, navy and teal typography, and large gold mathematical plates, while mathematical expressions are also recorded in searchable source notation and a separate Excel reference index. This is a prospective, nonclinical research architecture. It does not report new patient experiments, demonstrate safe autonomous human neurovascular microrobots, establish a universal device-migration system, or claim continuity of private thoughts, consciousness, or personal identity. Scientific benefit remains conditional on explicit task definitions, qualified device evidence, legitimate permissions, external validation, and the successor's freedom to reject a failed bridge. Research question: What should remain invariant when an interface changes, and who has the authority to say that its meaning has changed?

summary: Version 2.0 is a substantive revision of version 1.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.19174862). It supersedes the earlier procedural interpretation and its exclusion of competing explanations. The revised title is Structural Organization and Interpretive Limits of the Phaistos Disc. Reproduced descriptive findings are retained; failed model comparisons and photographic uncertainties are reported explicitly. The earlier version remains available through the record version history. We examine whether reproducible structural observations on the Phaistos Disc support a procedural interpretation. A pinned numerical transcription contains 242 main-sign positions, including one unreadable position, 45 readable sign types, 61 divider-defined groups and 18 supplementary stroke annotations. Source review reconciles counting and numbering conventions while retaining unresolved photographic uncertainty. The 02-to-12 side contrast persists after exact-family collapse. Adding side to a fixed position-only pairing predictor improves held-family loss by 0.082738 nats, but its exact conditional tail of 0.075 fails the frozen support rule. A positional mixture fails to outperform a bigram baseline. A separate directional test of the proposed 07-to-27 recovery relationship fails, with a one-sided permutation tail of 0.884. Supplementary-stroke comparisons have insufficient controlled overlap for the specified exact test. The work documents organization and constrains specific interpretations without establishing procedural functions or phonetic values. Corpus, code, protocols, full results and uncertainty ledgers accompany the paper.
title: Structural Organization and Interpretive Limits of the Phaistos Disc

summary: The Voynich Manuscript exhibits strong statistical regularities, but the distinction between recoverable grammar and recoverable lexical meaning remains unresolved. This study asks how far a progressively frozen, cross-validated analysis can reconstruct the manuscript’s internal word-building system without assigning meanings from illustrations, candidate languages, or post-hoc English paraphrase. Using canonical transcription, protected holdout partitions, alternate-transcription replication, exact host substitutions, and adversarial stopping rules, the analysis recovers a cumulative left-edge morphology, a transferable inventory of 39 surface CORE-0 stem/bodies, reproducible host-by-right-state coupling, a stable K/T referential contrast, and a directed network among powered lexical cores. The 39-core inventory predicts protected-frame combinatorics and content-blind contextual fingerprints out of sample, while attempts to decompose these bodies into a deeper transferable root layer fail. Nine recurring hosts show strongly replicated coupling to EY/EEY/EDY right-edge states, supporting a distributed morphological paradigm rather than independent left- and right-side systems. A 28-node directed CORE network also replicates across canonical calibration, untouched Holdout, and alternate-transcription tests, yielding neutral outbound- and inbound-biased stem classes without requiring part-of-speech or semantic assignments. On the project’s fully constrained 1,609-line benchmark, 12,299 of 12,495 positions are role-naturalizable (98.4314%), leaving 196 opaque positions. This percentage is explicitly a conditional benchmark-maturity statistic, not a measure of literal plaintext recovery or manuscript-wide translation accuracy. Repeated attempts to cross from structural organization to ordinary lexical meaning—including deeper-root induction, topic clustering, functional-neighborhood anchoring, local lexical syntax, illustration matching, source-language fitting, and prospective semantic transfer—fail the project’s promotion criteria. The resulting contribution is therefore a structural decipherment rather than a lexical one: a reproducible grammatical and morphological architecture together with an empirically identified lexical-identifiability ceiling. The work extends, but is distinct from, the earlier controlled-translation release at DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22049207.
title: Structural Decipherment Without Lexical Recovery: A Cross-Validated Morphological Analysis of the Voynich Manuscript

summary: This repository provides the official reproduction software, numerical simulation datasets, and empirical input fixtures for the manuscript: Song, X., Xu, H., & Bai, Y. (2026). Width Oscillations Regulate Event-Driven Bank Collapse and Point-Bar Growth in Transitional Meanders. Journal of Geophysical Research: Earth Surface. ( Under Review ) ABSTRACT Alluvial meanders dynamically adjust their planform and channel geometry, yet classical meander theory assumes a spatially uniform, constant channel width and continuous bank retreat, failing to capture episodic bank collapse and non-uniform width adjustments in transitional meandering rivers. Situated along the geomorphic continuum between single-thread and wandering streams, transitional meanders exhibit pronounced spatial width variations that break cross-sectional symmetry. Here, we develop a physically closed, reduced-complexity morphodynamic framework coupling a three-parameter asymptotic expansion of the three-dimensional Reynolds-averaged flow equations, continuous basal toe scour with transient pore-water suction, threshold-governed cantilever limit equilibrium, and a mass-conserving sediment partition driving inner point-bar progradation. The formulation demonstrates that the spatial phase relationship between channel width oscillations and centerline curvature steers the spatial displacement of outer-bank shear stress hotspots: channel constriction upstream of the bend apex amplifies cutbank shear stress, whereas channel expansion decelerates flow and promotes point-bar accretion. Discrete slump-block deposits provide self-adaptive hydraulic shielding that stabilizes the toe and regulates decadal channel relaxation. Hindcasting the 40-year morphodynamic evolution of the transitional Powder River, Montana, across 34 monumented cross sections reproduces post-flood channel widening and subsequent multi-decadal recovery narrowing across 228 discrete collapse events, while in the limit of uniform width the model recovers classical constant-width meander theory with first-order convergence along the meandering Juruá River. Global parameter sweeps quantitatively encompass observed erosion-to-accretion balance ratios across 84 worldwide natural rivers, providing a multiscale morphodynamic framework that links event-scale geotechnical failure to multi-decadal width evolution in alluvial channels. summary: Added fit_xy(model, x, y, theta0, sigmas, x_sigmas, max_iter=200, tol=1e-12) : the fit when the settings have error bars too (errors in variables), for any Model whose prediction for a measurement depends only on its own settings. Model: a pure source per pair (no law between pump power and gain assumed), the jitter law of phase_noise_variance , then the efficiency and a stated dark noise as in detected_variance . Checked against the package's own forward path (the output of single_mode_parametric behind an escape efficiency, at three analysis frequencies, is exactly such a source: efficiency to 1e-8, jitter to a relative 1e-6), against infer_source for one pair without jitter (relative 1e-10), and by 150 seeded noisy sets (scatter 0.75 to 1.3 times the error bars). The analysis follows how experiments describe loss and jitter, for example B. Shajilal et al., arXiv:2211.06632 (2022), who model their squeezing and antisqueezing against pump power with a total efficiency and a jitter angle. summary: PyUL_SK is the fork of PyUltraLight 2 used for the black-hole simulations of Stone Skipping Black Holes in Ultralight Dark Matter Solitons (A. Zhang, Y. Wang, J. L. Zagorac and R. Easther, arXiv:2602.11512 ). It is a pseudo-spectral (split-step Fourier) solver for the Schroedinger-Poisson equations of ultralight dark matter coupled to N-body point masses (black holes), with cell-centred grids, manual dynamical friction, isolated or periodic potentials, a resampled centre-of-mass cube for eigenmode analysis, and an optional inline decomposition into soliton eigenmodes, c_nlm(t), computed while the simulation runs (with the companion ULDM-Eigenmode-Toolkit). Release 30.50 is a maintenance release of the 30.40 core used for part of the paper runs. With default options it reproduces 30.40 bit for bit, except the resampled-cube outputs, which LegacyResampleBox=True reproduces. It adds packaging, tests, laptop and PBS/Slurm examples, support for Python 3.9 to 3.14 with NumPy 2 and current SciPy, safe non-interactive behaviour on clusters, complete provenance records, and many bug fixes. CHANGELOG.md lists every change; docs/known_issues_and_errata.md documents the bugs of older versions and their effect on the paper's figures. Lineage and credits: PyUltraLight by F. Edwards, E. Kendall, S. Hotchkiss and R. Easther (JCAP 10 (2018) 027, doi:10.1088/1475-7516/2018/10/027); PyUltraLight 2 / PyUL_NBody by Yourong F. Wang and collaborators (Auckland Cosmology; github.com/Sifyrena/PyUL_NBody , doi:10.5281/zenodo.6336160), on which this fork is built; SK fork by Alan Zhang. The NOTICE file records the origin of the code and reproduces the upstream BSD-style copyright notice; the fork's own changes are distributed under the MIT licence in LICENSE. Please also cite the upstream works and the paper listed in CITATION.cff.

summary: Water-supply licences in low- and middle-income jurisdictions routinely omit sanitation-service conditions, yet regulators and courts treat the resulting silence as though it were a neutral allocation of responsibility rather than an affirmative regulatory choice with distributive consequences. The analysis distinguishes three doctrinal mechanisms through which silence operates: expressio unius reasoning that confines regulatory duties to enumerated conditions; statutory gap-filling that imports sanitation obligations from adjacent water and public-health statutes; and standing doctrine that determines whether unserved peri-urban households can compel performance. Licence silence is not doctrinally inert but functions as a standing-allocation device: where the licence is silent, enforcement standing defaults to the regulator, and households in unserved peri-urban areas lack a doctrinal pathway to compel sanitation-service provision. The comparative analysis identifies a remedial asymmetry between jurisdictions that treat licence conditions as exhaustive and those that permit statutory implication, and proposes a doctrinal test for reading sanitation-service conditions into water-supply licences that preserves regulatory discretion while creating a justiciable pathway for unserved households. The contribution is a doctrinal framework linking licence drafting to enforcement standing, with implications for licence-condition design and for the justiciability of sanitation-service claims in peri-urban contexts.

summary: This repository provides the datasets, pretrained models and generated network parameters used in the manuscript “DiffPINN: Generative diffusion-initialized physics-informed neural networks for accelerating seismic wavefield representation.” The accompanying source code is publicly available at: https://github.com/DeepWave-KAUST/DiffPINN-pub DiffPINN is a latent diffusion framework that generates initialization parameters for physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) used in frequency-domain seismic wavefield modeling. A set of PINNs is first trained across diverse velocity models and their parameters are flattened into one-dimensional vectors. An autoencoder compresses the length of these vectors into multi-channel latent tensors, and a conditional diffusion model is trained on those tensors with the velocity model and source configuration as conditions. At inference, the diffusion model generates a latent tensor for a new velocity model, with a physics-based gradient correction applied at each reverse step, and the decoder turns it into a complete set of PINN parameters. The archived files are organized as follows. dataset.zip After extraction, dataset.zip contains five folders corresponding to the five stages of the framework: metatrain/ : contains meta_train.mat , the dataset used for meta-training. pinntrain/ : contains pinntrain1.mat to pinntrain2600.mat , one file per velocity model, used to train the 2600 PINNs that form the parameter dataset. aetrain/ : contains the flattened parameters of the 2600 converged PINNs, used to train the autoencoder. difftrain/ : contains the latent tensors encoded from those parameters, used to train the diffusion model. pinntest/ : contains CurveVelA.mat , Layer.mat and FlatFaultA.mat , the three test velocity models used to reproduce the results reported in the manuscript. All data are stored in MATLAB .mat format. Each .mat file contains the following variables: x_train , z_train , sx_train : the spatial coordinates and source locations of the collocation samples. m_train , m0_train : the squared slowness of the medium and of the homogeneous background. u0_real_train , u0_imag_train : the real and imaginary parts of the analytical background wavefield. x_test , z_test , sx_test : the coordinates of the full evaluation grid. du_real_test , du_imag_test : the real and imaginary parts of the numerical reference solution. The training velocity models are drawn from the CurveVel-A class of the OpenFWI benchmark dataset, resized to 101×101 with a grid spacing of 25 m and mildly smoothed. All wavefields are computed at 5 Hz. The reference solutions are obtained with the optimized nine-point frequency-domain finite-difference scheme of Jo et al. (1996). Among the three test models, CurveVelA is drawn from the training distribution, while Layer (a layered section of the Marmousi model) and FlatFaultA lie outside it. Because aetrain/ and difftrain/ are the outputs of the two preceding stages, users can start at any point in the pipeline rather than rebuilding the parameter dataset, which takes roughly 65 hours on ten V100 GPUs. trained_model.zip After extraction, trained_model.zip contains the three trained models used to reproduce the results in the manuscript: meta_trained.pth : the meta-learned PINN initialization, trained for 40000 iterations over 500 velocity models. ae_trained.pth : the autoencoder, trained for 1000 epochs on the 2600 flattened parameter vectors. diff_trained.pt : the conditional diffusion model, trained for 400000 iterations on the latent tensors. generated_weight.zip After extraction, generated_weight.zip contains the latent tensors generated by the trained diffusion model for the three test velocity models: CurveVelA_weight.mat : generated parameters for the in-distribution CurveVel-A model. Layer_weight.mat : generated parameters for the layered Marmousi model. FlatFaultA_weight.mat : generated parameters for the FlatFault-A model. These were produced
title: Dataset and Trained Models for "DiffPINN: Generative diffusion-initialized physics-informed neural networks for accelerating seismic wavefield representation"
